citation: Identification of key genes and immune infiltration modulated by CPAP in obstructive sleep apnea by integrated bioinformatics analysis (PMID: 34529670)
sample_size: PBMC transcriptomes from OSA patients before and after CPAP (GEO GSE133601); exact n not stated in abstract
significance: Module-trait correlation described as significant (no value given); random forest AUC 0.92
summary: In a WGCNA of PBMC transcriptomes (GSE133601) from OSA patients before and after CPAP treatment, H2BC8 fell in the black module, which correlated significantly with CPAP treatment. It was one of eleven hub genes (with TRAV10, RPL10, CD22, DNASE1L3 and others) used in a random forest model predicting CPAP efficacy (AUC 0.92). The hub genes partly correlated with monocyte infiltration, which was associated with OSA remission.

citation: Elucidating the role of Pyroptosis in papillary thyroid cancer: prognostic, immunological, and therapeutic perspectives (PMID: 38287330)
sample_size: TCGA PTC cohort; 6 external datasets, 16 cell lines, 20 paired clinical samples
significance: Nomogram outperformed four clinical staging systems (no specific p-value given for H2BC8)
summary: H2BC8 was one of nine pyroptosis-related genes (with CXCL8, GJA1, IFI27, PRDM1, PYCARD, SEZ6L2, SIGLEC15 and TRAF6) selected for the PyroScore prognostic model of thyroid cancer-free interval in papillary thyroid cancer (TCGA). The PyroScore was linked to tumor immune microenvironment remodeling and to predicted responses to immunotherapy, chemotherapy, RAI and targeted therapy. Expression of the prognostic genes was validated in six external datasets, 16 cell lines and 20 paired clinical samples.

citation: Anon. 2025 - ERV3-MLT1 provides cis-regulatory elements for human placental functioning and are commonly dysregulated in human-specific preeclampsia (PMID: 41188995)
summary: An upstream MLT1(G1) ERV element acts as an enhancer for EPS8L1, shown by reporter assay and genome editing. EPS8L1 is expressed in progenitor cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts and is overexpressed in preeclampsia. A soluble form is detectable in maternal plasma from about 24 weeks. EPS8L1 knockout in trophoblasts is lethal in vitro, and overexpression alters trophoblast behaviors characteristic of preeclampsia.

citation: Structural basis of PxxDY motif recognition in SH3 binding (PMID: 18644376)
summary: NMR solution structure of the Eps8L1 SH3 domain bound to the CD3epsilon PPVPNPDYEPIR peptide. Eps8L1 SH3 recognizes a PxxDY motif rather than canonical PxxP. Ile531 and Arg512 (salt bridge to D7) and E496 (hydrogen bond to Y8) determine this specificity.

citation: Reciprocal regulation of SH3 and SH2 domain binding via tyrosine phosphorylation of a common site in CD3epsilon (PMID: 17617578)
summary: A phage display screen identified Eps8L1 as a preferred SH3 partner of the CD3epsilon proline-rich region, together with Nck1/2. Binding maps to the PxxDY motif and is abolished by phosphorylation of Y166. In Jurkat T cells, TCR ligation induces Eps8L1 binding to endogenous CD3epsilon, and Y166 phosphorylation causes loss of that binding.

citation: The eps8 family of proteins links growth factor stimulation to actin reorganization generating functional redundancy in the Ras/Rac pathway (PMID: 14565974)
summary: Eps8L1 interacts with Abi1 and Sos-1, activates the Rac-GEF activity of Sos-1, and binds actin in vivo. It localizes to PDGF-induced F-actin-rich ruffles. Expressing it in eps8-/- fibroblasts restores RTK-mediated actin remodeling, which indicates functional redundancy with Eps8 in the Ras/Rac pathway.

citation: Comparative immunohistochemical analysis suggests a conserved role of EPS8L1 in epidermal and hair follicle barriers of mammals (PMID: 37889356)
summary: EPS8L1 mRNA is co-expressed with filaggrin and loricrin in terminally differentiated human keratinocytes. The protein is found in the epidermal granular layer and the hair follicle inner root sheath across mammals, partly at cell membranes. The gene has been lost in birds, and the pattern suggests a role in skin barrier function.

citation: Immunolocalization of Pglyrp3 and Eps8l1 proteins in the regenerating lizard epidermis indicates they contribute to epidermal barrier formation (PMID: 36854226)
summary: Eps8l is accumulated in the wound epidermis and in the shedding layer of regenerating lizard tail scales. This suggests a possible role in epidermal barrier formation or regeneration, but its function remains unknown.

citation: Gene expression profile associated with Asmt knockout-induced depression-like behaviors and exercise effects in mouse hypothalamus (PMID: 35771226)
summary: Eps8l1 was one of the differentially expressed genes in the hypothalamus of Asmt knockout mice with depression-like behavior, and also after swimming exercise. The change was partly confirmed by qRT-PCR.

citation: Effects of Tcte1 knockout on energy chain transportation and spermatogenesis: implications for male infertility (PMID: 38650655)
sample_size: Mouse WT, Tcte1+/- and Tcte1-/- males; 248 infertile human males screened for TCTE1
summary: Eps8l1 is identified as Drc3, a component of the nexin-dynein regulatory complex (N-DRC), and was visualized by immunofluorescence in mouse sperm. In Tcte1-/- males, N-DRC components including Eps8l1 were not transported to the sperm flagella.

citation: Feature Genes in Neuroblastoma Distinguishing High-Risk and Non-high-Risk Neuroblastoma Patients: Development and Validation Combining Random Forest With Artificial Neural Network (PMID: 35911385)
sample_size: GSE49710 training set; GSE73517 validation set
summary: EPS8L1 was selected by random forest as a feature differentially expressed gene distinguishing high-risk from non-high-risk neuroblastoma. It was part of a 5-gene model with high classification accuracy.

citation: Proteomics and Metabolic Characteristics of Boar Seminal Plasma Extracellular Vesicles Reveal Biomarker Candidates Related to Sperm Motility (PMID: 39067049)
summary: EPS8L1 was one of seven differentially expressed proteins in boar seminal plasma extracellular vesicles between high and low sperm motility groups. This marks it as a candidate biomarker of sperm motility.

citation: Straub et al. 2018 - Missense Variants in RHOBTB2 Cause a Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy in Humans, and Altered Levels Cause Neurological Defects in Drosophila (PMID: 29276004)
sample_size: 10 individuals with de novo BTB-domain missense variants
summary: Elevated levels of the Drosophila ortholog RhoBTB in vivo caused seizure susceptibility and severe locomotor defects. RhoBTB knockdown in dendritic arborization neurons reduced dendrite number, suggesting a role in dendritic development. In HEK293 cells, BTB-domain missense mutants of RHOBTB2 were more abundant than wild-type, probably because of impaired proteasomal degradation.

citation: Belal et al. 2018 - De novo variants in RHOBTB2, an atypical Rho GTPase gene, cause epileptic encephalopathy (PMID: 29768694)
summary: In Neuro-2a cells, three de novo RHOBTB2 mutants were more abundant than wild-type. CUL3 coexpression reduced wild-type RHOBTB2 but not the mutants, indicating impaired CUL3-dependent degradation. Precise regulation of RHOBTB2 levels appears essential for normal brain function.

citation: Mutant-specific dysfunction of RHOBTB2 impairs mitochondrial function and Na(+)/K(+)-ATPase levels in a cell model (PMID: 41478322)
summary: In a doxycycline-inducible cell model, hotspot mutants (R461H, R485C, R489Q) raised RHOBTB2 protein levels with nuclear and mitochondrial accumulation. R489Q downregulated ion channel genes in RNA-seq. Mutants reduced Na+/K+-ATPase via lysosomal degradation, and R489Q and W217C impaired mitochondrial respiration. The cancer-associated Y284D mutant did not share these phenotypes.

citation: Berthold et al. 2004 - RhoBTB2 is a substrate of the mammalian Cul3 ubiquitin ligase complex (PMID: 15107402)
summary: RhoBTB2 binds Cul3 through its first BTB domain and is a substrate of a Cul3-based ubiquitin ligase in vitro and in vivo. A lung cancer missense mutant cannot bind Cul3 and escapes proteasomal regulation, so its protein levels rise. Rhobtb2 is homozygously deleted in 3.5% of primary breast cancers, and its expression is lost in about 50% of breast and lung cancer cell lines.

citation: Hsp90-dependent assembly of the DBC2/RhoBTB2-Cullin3 E3-ligase complex (PMID: 24608665)
summary: DBC2/RhoBTB2 is an Hsp90 client protein that associates with Hsp90 and its co-chaperones in reticulocyte lysate and MCF7 cells. It retains GTP binding, which is modulated by the Hsp90 ATPase cycle. Assembly of the DBC2-Cullin3-COP9 E3 ligase complex depends on Hsp90.

citation: DBC2/RhoBTB2 functions as a tumor suppressor protein via Musashi-2 ubiquitination in breast cancer (PMID: 27941885)
summary: A cDNA-library in vitro ubiquitination screen identified Musashi-2 (MSI2) as a DBC2 substrate. DBC2 binds MSI2 directly and promotes its polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, suppressing MSI2-linked oncogenic functions and inducing apoptosis. DBC2 and MSI2 protein levels are inversely correlated in breast tissue microarrays.

citation: RhoBTB Proteins Regulate the Hippo Pathway by Antagonizing Ubiquitination of LKB1 (PMID: 32111652)
summary: RhoBTB depletion in the Drosophila wing disc cooperated with Yki to drive neoplasia. RhoBTB2 depletion in human cells raised YAP activity and increased anchorage-independent colony formation. It also reduced LKB1 protein and increased LKB1 ubiquitination, and restoring LKB1 rescued RhoBTB loss in Drosophila.

citation: RHOBTB2 enhances cell proliferation of acute myeloid leukemia by modulating Hippo-YAP1 signaling and dependent of KLHL13 (PMID: 41107424)
sample_size: KG-1 and MOLM-13 AML cell lines
summary: RHOBTB2 is upregulated in AML and tracks with poor prognosis. In KG-1 and MOLM-13 cells, overexpression increased proliferation and migration and suppressed apoptosis, while silencing had the opposite effects. RHOBTB2 binds KLHL13 (co-IP) and stabilizes it by blocking proteasomal degradation, acting through Hippo-YAP1 signaling.

citation: Freeman et al. 2007 - RhoBTB2 (DBC2) is a mitotic E2F1 target gene with a novel role in apoptosis (PMID: 18039672)
summary: RHOBTB2 is a direct transcriptional target of E2F1: E2F1 overexpression raised its mRNA and protein, and E2F1 knockdown lowered its protein. Expression is strongly upregulated in mitosis and during drug-induced apoptosis, partly depending on E2F1. RHOBTB2 knockdown delayed drug-induced apoptosis.

citation: RhoBTB2 gene in breast cancer is silenced by promoter methylation (PMID: 24356943)
sample_size: 50 paired breast cancer and normal tissues
summary: RhoBTB2 promoter methylation and mRNA downregulation were found in breast tumor tissue compared with matched normal tissue. Methylated samples had lower mRNA, and methylation was enriched in progesterone receptor-negative tumors.

citation: 2025 - SEPTIN7 Deficiency Disrupts Endothelial Integrity and Causes Myxomatous Valve Disease in Juvenile Mice (PMID: 42657464)
phenotype: Endocardial lineage-specific Septin2 conditional knockout mice developed normally with no detectable abnormalities; No cardiac/valve phenotype detected in Septin2 cKO (in contrast to Septin7 cKO, which showed juvenile lethality from aortic stenosis and myxomatous valve degeneration)

citation: 2025 - Hypoxia exposure impairs male fertility via inhibiting Septin2-mediated spermatogonial proliferation (PMID: 40487848)
phenotype: Sept2 knockdown in normoxic mice phenocopied hypoxia-induced defects in spermatogenesis; Impaired spermatogonial proliferation; G1-S phase arrest upon Sept2 depletion in spermatogonial cells in vitro; Sept2 loss stabilized PP2A B56γ and enhanced AKT dephosphorylation; Hypoxia-induced Sept2 downregulation associated with reduced sperm quality and fertility

citation: Toriyama et al. 2017 - Folate-dependent methylation of septins governs ciliogenesis during neural tube closure (PMID: 28432198)
summary: Embryos with neural tube defects failed to adequately methylate septin2, a regulator of cilium structure and function. Folate-dependent methylation of septin2 affects its GTP binding and formation of the septin2-6-7 complex, linking the folate/1-carbon pathway to ciliogenesis and neural tube closure.

citation: Septin2 mediates podosome maturation and endothelial cell invasion associated with angiogenesis (PMID: 31865373)
summary: Septin2, Septin6 and Septin7 are required for maturation of endothelial podosomes into matrix-degrading organelles. Septin2 is recruited after Tks5 and F-actin and localizes around the podosome perimeter. Its phosphoinositide-binding residues are required for podosome function and for endothelial invasion in angiogenesis.

citation: S-Nitrosylation of Septin2 Exacerbates Aortic Aneurysm and Dissection by Coupling the TIAM1-RAC1 Axis in Macrophages (PMID: 38357802)
summary: Septin2 is S-nitrosylated at Cys111 in aortic tissue from dissection patients and Ang II-infused Apoe-/- mice. SNO-Septin2 shows reduced interaction with TIAM1, which activates the TIAM1-RAC1 axis and NF-κB signaling. This drives macrophage inflammation and extracellular matrix degradation. RAC1 inhibition with R-Ketorolac or NSC23766 was protective.

citation: SEPTIN2 suppresses an IFN-γ-independent, proinflammatory macrophage activation pathway (PMID: 37978190)
summary: ER stress induces SEPT2 expression. SEPT2 balances acetylation versus ubiquitination of HSPA5 (BiP) at Lys327, which alleviates ER stress and limits M1-like polarization and proinflammatory cytokine release. Disrupting this feedback leads to unfolded protein accumulation and excessive inflammation.

citation: Hypoxia exposure impairs male fertility via inhibiting Septin2-mediated spermatogonial proliferation (PMID: 40487848)
sample_size: 24 high-altitude residents, 6 pathological hypoxia patients, 19 controls; mouse n=3-5 per group
summary: Hypoxia downregulates Sept2 transcription in spermatogonia by disrupting POLR2A binding to the Sept2 promoter. Reduced Sept2 stabilizes PP2A B56γ, which dephosphorylates AKT and causes G1-S arrest. Sept2 knockdown phenocopied hypoxia-induced spermatogenesis defects in mice, and Sept2 overexpression rescued proliferation.

citation: Lysyl hydroxylase LH1 promotes confined migration and metastasis of cancer cells by stabilizing Septin2 to enhance actin network (PMID: 36721170)
summary: LH1 binds and stabilizes SEPT2 in a hydroxylase domain-dependent manner, which enhances actin polymerization and confined migration and metastasis in HCC and PDAC. Patients with high expression of both LH1 and SEPT2 had the poorest prognosis.

citation: Functional interdependence between septin and actin cytoskeleton (PMID: 15541171)
summary: Septin2 filaments associate with actin bundles but are excluded from dynamic leading edges and ruffles. FRAP showed Septin2 assemblies are highly dynamic independent of actin. RNAi and truncation constructs showed Septin2 stabilizes or maintains actin bundles.

citation: FHL2-driven molecular network mediated Septin2 knockdown inducing apoptosis in mesangial cell (PMID: 25103794)
summary: FHL2 was identified as a new Septin2 interaction partner. Septin2 knockdown induced mesangial cell apoptosis via FHL2-mediated p-ERK1 and p-AKT signaling, and FHL2 overexpression alleviated this effect. Septin2 and FHL2 expression were linked to apoptosis in the anti-Thy1 nephritis rat model.

citation: Septin2 regulates ARHGAP25-mediated suppression of lamellipodia formation and cell spreading (PMID: 40205813)
summary: Septin2 interacts with ARHGAP25, a Rac GAP, and colocalizes with it at lamellipodia. Septin2 depletion relieved ARHGAP25-mediated suppression of lamellipodia and spreading, whereas septin2 overexpression enhanced the suppression, so septin2 regulates Rac signaling through ARHGAP25.

citation: Septin2 is modified by SUMOylation and required for chromosome congression in mouse oocytes (PMID: 20372094)
summary: Septin2 is SUMO-1 modified in mouse oocytes and localizes along the metaphase spindle and at the midbody. Inhibitor or siRNA disruption of septins caused metaphase I/anaphase I arrest, chromosome misalignment and spindle checkpoint activation (BubR1), but did not affect cytokinesis.

citation: Zebrafish dscaml1 Deficiency Impairs Retinal Patterning and Oculomotor Function (PMID: 31685652)
phenotype: Deficits in retinal patterning and light adaptation; Severe fatigue during gaze stabilization; Reduced saccade amplitude and velocity in the light; Greater eye disconjugacy; Impaired fixation; Impaired saccade-command signals in abducens neurons (saccadic premotor pathway); Normal abducens activation by the pretectum-vestibular pathway; Phenotypes reminiscent of human ocular motor apraxia

citation: Fuerst et al. 2009 - DSCAM and DSCAML1 function in self-avoidance in multiple cell types in the developing mouse retina (PMID: 19945391)
phenotype: Dscaml1 mutant retina: fasciculated rod bipolar cell dendrites; Dscaml1 mutant retina: clumped AII amacrine cell bodies, indicating a self-avoidance defect; Appropriate stratification of neurites in inner plexiform layer synaptic laminae; Functional synapses formed in the rod circuit; Dscam-/- mice: RGC dendrite fasciculation and clumped cell bodies

citation: The rod synapse in aging wildtype and Dscaml1 mutant mice (PMID: 37910517)
phenotype: Rod-to-rod bipolar cell synapses form and are maintained; Increased number of invaginating neurites in rod spherules; Reduced rod bipolar cell dendritic tips; Reduced mitochondrial volume and complexity in rod bipolar cells; Precocious sprouting of rod bipolar cell dendrites into the outer nuclear layer

citation: Subtle Roles of Down Syndrome Cell Adhesion Molecules in Embryonic Forebrain Development and Neuronal Migration (PMID: 33585465)
phenotype: Constitutive loss of Dscaml1 (Dscaml1 GT) and Dscam did not significantly affect cortical development; No significant effect on ventral forebrain morphogenesis; No significant effect on cortical interneuron migration; No significant effect on cortical-subcortical connectivity formation; Gain of function impaired neural migration and altered neuronal morphology

citation: Deficiency in the cell-adhesion molecule dscaml1 impairs hypothalamic CRH neuron development and perturbs normal neuroendocrine stress axis function (PMID: 36875755)
phenotype: Higher crhb expression in hypothalamic CRH neurons; Increased CRH neuron cell number; Reduced cell death in CRH neurons; Higher baseline cortisol levels; Attenuated cortisol responses to acute stressors; Dysregulated HPA axis

citation: Pharmacological Correction of Aberrant DSCAML1 Localization by 4-Phenylbutyrate Ameliorates Epileptic Phenotypes in a Mouse Model Harboring the Patient-Specific A2105T Mutation (PMID: 42003794)
phenotype: Dscaml1 A2105T/A2105T knock-in: mutant protein accumulates intracellularly and is not properly localized to the cell surface; Dendritic retraction in cortical layer V pyramidal neurons; Abnormal clustering of somatostatin-positive interneurons in the hippocampus; Epileptic spike-and-wave discharges; 4PBA restored cell-surface localization and ameliorated neuronal deficits and reduced spike-and-wave discharge frequency

citation: Structural Neural Connectivity Analysis in Zebrafish With Restricted Anterograde Transneuronal Viral Labeling and Quantitative Brain Mapping (PMID: 32038180)
phenotype: Differences in topographical distribution of retinofugal connectivity patterns in dscaml1 mutants compared with wild type

citation: Zebrafish dscaml1 Deficiency Impairs Retinal Patterning and Oculomotor Function (PMID: 31685652)
summary: Zebrafish dscaml1 mutants showed deficits in retinal patterning and light adaptation. They also had oculomotor deficits (fatigue during gaze stabilization, reduced saccade amplitude and velocity, impaired fixation). Calcium imaging of abducens neurons showed impaired saccade-command signals, which suggests a defect in the saccadic premotor pathway. The phenotype resembles human ocular motor apraxia.

citation: Tyrosine phosphorylation is essential for DSCAML1 to promote dendrite arborization of mouse cortical neurons (PMID: 24084194)
summary: Knockdown of DSCAML1 in newborn mouse cortical neurons caused dendritic fasciculation and increased self-crossing, which impairs self-avoidance. The phosphorylation-deficient DSCAML1 Y1808F mutant failed to rescue the defect, so Y1808 phosphorylation is required for DSCAML1 function.

citation: DSCAM and DSCAML1 regulate the radial migration and callosal projection in developing cerebral cortex (PMID: 25451118)
summary: RNAi knockdown of DSCAML1 in mouse cortical neurons in vitro increased proximal dendritic branching complexity and impeded axon growth. In vivo knockdown impaired radial migration and callosal projection.

citation: DSCAM and DSCAML1 function in self-avoidance in multiple cell types in the developing mouse retina (PMID: 19945391)
summary: Dscaml1 is expressed in the rod circuit. Dscaml1-null mice had fasciculated rod bipolar cell dendrites and clumped AII amacrine cell bodies, which indicates a role in self-avoidance. Laminar stratification and rod-circuit synapse formation were intact, so Dscaml1 is not essential for synaptic specificity.

citation: Nuclear import of the DSCAM-cytoplasmic domain drives signaling capable of inhibiting synapse formation (PMID: 30745319)
summary: The DSCAML1 intracellular domain binds the importin IPO5 directly through a conserved nuclear localization signal and translocates to the nucleus. Expressing the DSCAML1 ICD altered expression of genes for neuronal differentiation, apoptosis and synapse function, and impaired neurite growth in primary cortical neurons. Unlike the DSCAM ICD, it did not reduce synapse numbers.

citation: Cloning and functional characterization of DSCAML1, a novel DSCAM-like cell adhesion molecule that mediates homophilic intercellular adhesion (PMID: 11453658)
summary: DSCAML1 (chr 11q23) encodes 10 Ig and 6 FNIII domains. It is a cell-surface molecule with homophilic binding activity that does not require divalent cations. In mouse brain it is expressed predominantly in cerebellar Purkinje cells, dentate gyrus granule cells, cortical neurons and olfactory bulb. In PC12 cells it targets axonal features.

citation: Human down syndrome cell adhesion molecules (DSCAMs) are functionally conserved with Drosophila Dscam[TM1] isoforms in controlling neurodevelopment (PMID: 21645617)
summary: Human DSCAML1 partially rescued the larval lethality of Drosophila Dscam mutants. It was targeted to dendrites and preferentially rescued dendrite defects, which shows functional conservation with the Dscam[TM1] isoforms.

citation: Deficiency in the cell-adhesion molecule dscaml1 impairs hypothalamic CRH neuron development and perturbs normal neuroendocrine stress axis function (PMID: 36875755)
summary: Zebrafish dscaml1 mutants had hypothalamic CRH neurons with higher crhb expression, increased cell number and reduced cell death. They also had higher baseline cortisol and attenuated responses to acute stressors, which implicates dscaml1 in HPA stress axis development.

citation: Genetic effects of DSCAML1 identified in genome-wide association study revealing strong associations with litter size and semen quality in goat (PMID: 32036056)
summary: Goat DSCAML1 expression in testis differed between the mitotic and meiotic stages. Three indels were genotyped in 2162 Shaanbei White Cashmere goats. Two indels (P2-16bp, P14-15bp) were associated with sperm motility and density, and three loci were associated with first-birth litter size. Genotype also affected DSCAML1 expression.

citation: Expression patterns of dscam and sdk gene paralogs in developing zebrafish retina (PMID: 30078982)
summary: Zebrafish dscaml1 was expressed in the inner nuclear layer and ganglion cell layer of the developing retina. Some cells in the basal INL co-expressed dscaml1 and dscama.

citation: Hypomaturation enamel defects in Klk4 knockout/LacZ knockin mice (PMID: 19578120)
phenotype: Klk4 replaced by lacZ reporter (null allele); beta-galactosidase expressed in maturation-stage ameloblasts only; Retained enamel proteins in maturation-stage enamel; Enamel normal in thickness with decussating rods; Enamel rapidly abraded after weaning despite soft chow; Enamel fractured readily; crystallites failed to interlock; Delayed crystal maturation; Hypomaturation amelogenesis imperfecta

citation: Maturation stage enamel malformations in Amtn and Klk4 null mice (PMID: 26620968)
phenotype: Klk4-/- mice healthy and fertile with no abnormalities except in enamel; Chalky-white, chipped mandibular incisors; Enamel thickness, volume and rod decussation unchanged; Enamel maturation onset mesial to the normal position; Reduced enamel mineral density (2.5 vs 3.1 gHA/cm3 in wild type); Reduced Knoop hardness at all enamel levels; Amtn-/-Klk4-/- double null outer enamel softer than in either single null
significance: significantly reduced mineral density and hardness (p-values not given in abstract)

citation: Effect of kallikrein 4 loss on enamel mineralization: comparison with mice lacking matrix metalloproteinase 20 (PMID: 21454549)
phenotype: Enamel normal in thickness and layer/rod organization; Developmental defect in enamel rods near the dentinoenamel junction; Normal mineralization to early maturation, then retention and gain of protein; Enamel unable to mature beyond 85% mineral by weight; Hard outer enamel but soft, protein-rich inner enamel; Overall mineral acquisition rate reduced by 25%

citation: Enamel proteins and proteases in Mmp20 and Klk4 null and double-null mice (PMID: 22243248)
phenotype: Retained organic matrix in Klk4 null enamel; Secretory-stage matrix in Klk4 null identical to wild type; Klk4 expression normal in Mmp20 null background, and a 40-kDa protease induced in Mmp20 null maturation stage; Mmp20/Klk4 double nulls retained more residual matrix than either single null; Limited functional redundancy between MMP20 and KLK4

citation: Relationships between protein and mineral during enamel development in normal and genetically altered mice (PMID: 22243238)
phenotype: Normal mineral acquisition up to early maturation in Klk4 null mice; Input of new volatiles (protein) in mid to late maturation; Final mineralization slowed below normal levels

citation: Direct and indirect mechanisms of KLK4 inhibition revealed by structure and dynamics (PMID: 27767076)
summary: X-ray crystal structures of KLK4 in complex with sunflower trypsin inhibitor-1 (SFTI-1) and an engineered SFTI-1 derivative were solved at ~1 Å resolution, and a structure with bound nickel was also solved. Together with MD simulations, they reveal a dynamic pathway between the metal-binding exosite and the active site, supporting an allosteric mode of inhibition.

citation: Kallikrein-related peptidase 4 induces cancer-associated fibroblast features in prostate-derived stromal cells (PMID: 28510269)
summary: KLK4 is highly expressed in prostate epithelium of PIN and malignant lesions, especially at the peristromal interface. In WPMY1 stromal cells, KLK4 activated PAR-1 and induced CAF-like features (increased αSMA, ESR1, SFRP1, FGF1, TAGLN, LOX, IL8, VEGFA). It also drove proliferation and secretome changes that stimulated HUVEC proliferation in a VEGFA-dependent manner.

citation: Substrates of the prostate-specific serine protease prostase/KLK4 defined by positional-scanning peptide libraries (PMID: 15389820)
summary: Recombinant KLK4 is a trypsin-like serine protease that prefers P1-Arg. Its predicted and tested substrates include pro-PSA/KLK3, which it activates, and IGFBP family members, which it degrades. Database searches also flagged PTHrP and BMP family members as candidate substrates. KLK4 is expressed in androgen-regulated prostate epithelium.

citation: Characterization of KLK4 expression and detection of KLK4-specific antibody in prostate cancer patient sera (PMID: 12370833)
summary: KLK4 mRNA and protein are expressed specifically in normal prostate and in primary and metastatic prostate tumors, with low-level mRNA in adrenal gland, salivary gland and thyroid. Prostate cancer patient sera contain antibodies that bind recombinant KLK4.

citation: KLK4 Silencing Inhibits the Growth of Chromophobe Renal Cell Carcinoma through ERK/AKT Signaling Pathway (PMID: 36260980)
summary: KLK4 is upregulated in kidney chromophobe tumors and cell lines. KLK4 knockdown reduced proliferation, colony formation, migration, invasion and EMT, and slowed xenograft tumor growth in nude mice, with lower Ki-67 and CD105. The abstract reports that AKT and ERK phosphorylation were enhanced with KLK4 silencing and concludes KLK4 acts via ERK/AKT signaling.

citation: KLK4 silencing inhibits the growth of oral squamous cell carcinoma through Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway (PMID: 28150891)
summary: KLK4 is highly expressed in OSCC. Silencing it inhibited proliferation and colony formation, caused cell cycle arrest and enhanced apoptosis (cleaved PARP, cleaved caspase-3 and Bax up, Bcl-2 down). It also reduced Wnt1, β-catenin, p-GSK-3β, cyclin D1 and c-myc, and a Wnt/β-catenin activator reversed the effects, placing KLK4 upstream of Wnt/β-catenin signaling.

citation: Maturation stage enamel malformations in Amtn and Klk4 null mice (PMID: 26620968)
significance: significantly reduced mineral density and hardness
summary: Klk4-/- mice have chalky, chipped incisors with reduced enamel mineral density (2.5 vs 3.1 gHA/cm3 in wild type) and reduced hardness at all enamel levels. Phenotypes of Amtn-/- and Klk4-/- mice differ, and the double knockout is additive, so AMTN and KLK4 function independently and both are needed for enamel maturation.

citation: Novel MMP20 and KLK4 Mutations in Amelogenesis Imperfecta (PMID: 26124219)
summary: Whole exome sequencing of consanguineous families identified a homozygous KLK4 frameshift (c.620_621delCT, p.Ser207Trpfs*38) causing recessive hypomaturation amelogenesis imperfecta. The mutant KLK4 was degraded intracellularly and was inactive.

citation: Molecular and circadian controls of ameloblasts (PMID: 22243224)
summary: In HAT-7 ameloblast cells, Klk4 (a maturation-stage marker) mRNA was upregulated by overexpression of both Dlx3 and Runx2. Amelx and Enam were instead down-regulated by Runx2 and up-regulated by Dlx3. Clock genes also influenced the rhythmic expression of ameloblast-specific genes and of Runx2.

citation: NaF reduces KLK4 expression by decreasing Foxo1/Runx2 expression in LS8 cells (PMID: 34781073)
summary: In LS8 ameloblast-like cells, NaF decreased Runx2 dose- and time-dependently. Runx2 knockdown markedly decreased KLK4 expression under NaF, and Foxo1 positively regulated Runx2, so a Foxo1/Runx2/KLK4 axis underlies low KLK4 in fluoride exposure.

citation: Ji et al. 2018 - Poly(C)-Binding Protein Pcbp2 Enables Differentiation of Definitive Erythropoiesis by Directing Functional Splicing of the Runx1 Transcript (PMID: 29866654)
phenotype: selective deficiency of the definitive erythroid lineage in Pcbp2-/- embryos; aberrant exclusion of Runx1 cassette exon 6 in the embryonic liver; Runx1ΔE6 homozygous embryos phenocopy the loss of the definitive erythroid lineage

citation: Zhang et al. 2016 - RNA-binding Protein PCBP2 Regulates p73 Expression and p73-dependent Antioxidant Defense (PMID: 26907686)
phenotype: PCBP2-deficient mice and primary MEFs show decreased p73 expression; increased ROS production in PCBP2-deficient MEFs; accelerated cellular senescence in PCBP2-deficient MEFs

citation: RNA-binding protein PCBP2 regulates pancreatic β cell function and adaptation to glucose (PMID: 38950317)
phenotype: Pcbp2-deficient β cells show impaired insulin secretion and adaptation to glucose; altered expression of mRNAs encoding insulin secretory pathway components; defects in calcium flux; abnormal insulin granule ultrastructure and exocytosis; defective amplification pathway of insulin secretion

citation: RNA binding proteins PCBP1 and PCBP2 regulate pancreatic β cell translation (PMID: 40451383)
phenotype: β cell-specific Pcbp1 deletion alone preserved glucose homeostasis; Pcbp1/2 β cell co-deletion caused severe diabetes due to compromised β cell viability; downregulation of translation initiation factor and ribosomal mRNAs in co-deficient β cells; reduced global mRNA translation

citation: Iron chaperones and RNA-binding proteins, PCBP1 and PCBP2, maintain hepatic iron balance and protect against ferroptosis (PMID: 42379276)
phenotype: Alb-Cre PCBP1/PCBP2 double deletion caused chronic severe hepatic injury with steatosis, necrosis and ductular reaction; increased plasma ALT and ALP; Nrf2-dependent antioxidant gene activation; AAV8-iCre double deletion in adult mice caused acute liver injury with periportal inflammation, apoptosis and DNA damage; ferroptosis-like injury with lipid peroxidation and 8-oxoguanine nucleic acid modifications; single PCBP2 deletion caused mild or no acute liver abnormalities (functional redundancy); dietary iron restriction improved liver pathology

citation: Role of PCBP2 in regulating nanovesicles loaded with curcumin to mitigate neuroferroptosis in neural damage caused by heat stroke (PMID: 39731111)
phenotype: PCBP2 silencing reversed the protective effect of NVs-CUR on hypothalamic neural injury in the heat stroke model; reduced survival and worsened nerve function deficit scores; increased ferroptosis and reduced SLC7A11 mRNA stability

citation: Silencing PCBP2 normalizes desmoplastic stroma and improves the antitumor activity of chemotherapy in pancreatic cancer (PMID: 33500719)
phenotype: PCBP2 siRNA nanocomplex reduced type I collagen and ECM production in stellate cells and NIH 3T3 fibroblasts; enhanced drug penetration through desmoplastic stroma; combined with gemcitabine, suppressed tumor progression in an orthotopic PDAC mouse model

citation: PCBP2 stabilizes TROAP to promote the malignant progression of gastric cancer (PMID: 39586843)
phenotype: PCBP2 knockdown repressed tumor growth of gastric cancer cells in a subcutaneous xenograft mouse model

citation: Wang et al. 2012 - Iron homeostasis regulates the activity of the microRNA pathway through poly(C)-binding protein 2 (PMID: 22633452)
summary: PCBP2 associates with Dicer and promotes processing of miRNA precursors. Cytosolic iron modulates PCBP2-Dicer association, PCBP2 multimerization and its binding to pre-miRNAs, so PCBP2 links iron homeostasis to miRNA biogenesis. Iron chelators activate the miRNA pathway.

citation: FAST-iCLIP 2014 - Dissecting noncoding and pathogen RNA-protein interactomes (PMID: 25411354)
summary: FAST-iCLIP of PCBP2 showed it binds CU-rich motifs in different topologies on mRNAs and noncoding RNAs with distinct biological functions. In HCV-infected cells it also mapped PCBP2 interactions with host and viral RNAs.

citation: Iron drives protease-independent cleavage of gasdermin D in allergic airway diseases (PMID: 42361797)
summary: PCBP2 acts as an iron chaperone that delivers iron directly to GSDMD. This triggers a localized Fenton reaction whose hydroxyl radicals cleave GSDMD to the active p40 fragment, enabling IL-33 release. Blocking this pathway reduced ILC2 activation and allergic airway inflammation in mice.

citation: PCBP2 knockdown promotes ferroptosis in malignant mesothelioma (PMID: 35089637)
sample_size: Rat and human MM specimens and cell lines
summary: PCBP2 knockdown, but not PCBP1 knockdown, decreased TfR1 and FTH expression and proliferation in mesothelioma cells. It also increased sensitivity to erastin-induced ferroptosis with increased catalytic Fe(II). Normal rat peritoneal mesothelium lacked PCBP2 immunopositivity, whereas ~90% of rat MM specimens were PCBP1/2 positive.

citation: RNA-binding protein PCBP2 regulates pancreatic β cell function and adaptation to glucose (PMID: 38950317)
summary: PCBP2 is induced by high glucose in mouse and human islets and is downregulated in islets from T2D donors. Pcbp2-deficient β cells showed altered insulin secretory pathway mRNAs, defective calcium flux, abnormal insulin granule ultrastructure and exocytosis, and impaired insulin secretion. PCBP2-affected genes overlapped with T2D-associated SNP-linked genes.

citation: PCBP2 Regulates p16(INK4a)-Dependent Cellular Senescence in Response to Iron (PMID: 41216990)
summary: The atherosclerosis-associated CDKN2A/B functional SNP rs1333046 recruits PCBP2 to regulate p16INK4a and senescence in endothelial cells. PCBP2 also regulates CD40 and NF-κB-driven SASP genes. Iron alters PCBP2 binding to rs1333046, and PCBP2 overexpression restores senescence in cells with reduced labile iron.

citation: PHGDH Inhibits Ferroptosis and Promotes Malignant Progression by Upregulating SLC7A11 in Bladder Cancer (PMID: 36147463)
summary: PHGDH binds PCBP2 (co-IP/mass spectrometry) and inhibits its ubiquitination-mediated degradation. Stabilized PCBP2 then stabilizes SLC7A11 mRNA, increasing SLC7A11 expression and suppressing ferroptosis in bladder cancer.

citation: PCBP2 Mediates Olaparib Resistance in Breast Cancer by Inhibiting m6A Methylation to Stabilize PARP1 mRNA (PMID: 40773674)
summary: PCBP2 is upregulated in olaparib-resistant BRCA-mutated breast cancer cells. PCBP2 overexpression increased resistance. PCBP2 directly binds PARP1 mRNA, inhibits its m6A methylation and stabilizes it, enhancing DNA repair.

citation: PCBP2 Posttranscriptional Modifications Induce Breast Cancer Progression via Upregulation of UFD1 and NT5E (PMID: 33037085)
summary: PCBP2 mRNA and protein levels are discordant in breast cancer. Alternative polyadenylation of the 3'UTR yields shorter transcripts that produce more protein. High PCBP2 protein is associated with progression and poor outcome. PCBP2 knockdown reduced proliferation, migration, invasion, tumor growth and metastasis. PCBP2 binds the 3'UTRs of UFD1 and NT5E to upregulate them.

citation: Pharmacologic inhibition of PCBP2 biomolecular condensates relieves Alzheimer's disease (PMID: 41298370)
summary: PCBP2 is elevated in the brains of AD patients and animal models and correlates with phase-separated condensates. These condensates sequester mitochondrial and mRNA-binding proteins, impair mitochondria, and promote BACE1 mRNA decay. The small molecule CN-0928 binds INTS1, reduces PCBP2 levels, and improves AD pathology and cognition.

citation: Epigenetics and autism spectrum disorder: A report of an autism case with mutation in H1 linker histone HIST1H1E and literature review (PMID: 29704315)
variant_detail: c.435dupC, p.Thr146Hisfs*50 (HIST1H1E/H1-4)
phenotype: autism spectrum disorder; intellectual disability
diagnostic_reason: De novo frameshift in the C-terminal domain that truncates the positively charged C-terminus; expression study showed reduced protein expression, supporting haploinsufficiency/loss of function; consistent with other reported HIST1H1E cases in intellectual disability

citation: Article 1 - The linker histone H1.4 condenses chromatin in maturing postmitotic neurons (PMID: 42619895)
phenotype: Developmental maturation of chromatin compaction in cerebellar granule neurons is disrupted in H1f2/H1f4 double knockout mice; H1.4 is robustly expressed in mature post-mitotic neurons throughout the brain; H1.4 accumulates in heterochromatin during neuronal maturation (ChIP)
knockout_type: other (H1f2/H1f4 double knockout; epitope-tagged H1f4 knock-in used for expression studies)

citation: Article 3 - Spermatogenesis proceeds normally in mice without linker histone H1t (PMID: 10933220)
phenotype: H1t-deficient mice developed normally with no anatomic abnormalities; Normal spermatogenesis and testicular morphology; H1.1, H1.2 and H1.4 gene expression enhanced during spermatogenesis in H1t-deficient mice (compensation)
knockout_type: other (H1t knockout, not H1-4; H1.4 expression assessed as compensatory change)

citation: Yusufova et al. 2021 - Histone H1 loss drives lymphoma by disrupting 3D chromatin architecture (PMID: 33299181)
summary: H1-4 (H1E) is recurrently mutated in B cell lymphomas, and lymphoma-associated H1 alleles act as driver mutations. Combined loss of H1c and H1e in mice caused chromatin decompaction, gain of H3K36me2 and/or loss of H3K27me3, and derepression of developmentally silenced stem cell genes. This enhanced germinal centre B cell fitness and led to aggressive lymphomas, establishing H1 as a tumour suppressor.

citation: Depletion of human histone H1 variants uncovers specific roles in gene expression and cell growth (PMID: 18927631)
summary: Inducible shRNA knockdown of H1.4 in T47D breast cancer cells caused cell death, the first evidence that an H1 variant is essential for survival in a human cell type. Other variants were not upregulated to compensate, and H1.4 depletion altered a distinct subset of genes by microarray.

citation: Linker histone H1.2 and H1.4 affect the neutrophil lineage determination (PMID: 32391789)
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen in PLB-985 cells and H1 subtype disruption showed that loss of H1.4 (with H1.2) induced an eosinophil-like transcriptional program. H1.4 therefore negatively regulates differentiation toward the neutrophil lineage, and H1 subtypes also affected the eosinophil bias of murine bone marrow stem cells.

citation: Linker Histone H1.4 Inhibits the Growth, Migration and EMT Process of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer by Regulating ERK1/2 Expression (PMID: 38472566)
summary: H1.4 overexpression in A549 and H1299 NSCLC cells inhibited viability, migration, invasion and EMT, whereas knockdown promoted them. H1.4 bound the ERK1/2 promoter and acted as a transcriptional repressor of ERK1/2, and ERK re-expression rescued the phenotypes.

citation: Ras-ERK signalling represses H1.4 phosphorylation at serine 36 to promote non-small-cell lung carcinoma cells growth and migration (PMID: 31184227)
summary: Ras-ERK signalling represses H1.4S36 phosphorylation through MDM2-mediated degradation of PKA. H1.4S36ph acts as a tumour suppressor: its overexpression reduced viability, colony formation, migration and invasion in NCI-H2126 and A549 cells, and it regulated transcription of Ras downstream genes.

citation: K-Ras(G12V/Y40C)-PI3K/AKT pathway regulates H1.4(S35ph) through PKA to promote the occurrence and development of osteosarcoma cancer (PMID: 31126199)
summary: In MG-63 osteosarcoma cells, RasG12V/Y40C-PI3K/AKT signalling lowered H1.4S35 phosphorylation by down-regulating PKA and up-regulating MDM2. The phosphomimetic H1.4S35E reduced viability, colony formation and migration, opposing the effects of Ras.

citation: CYP1B1 promotes PARPi-resistance via histone H1.4 interaction and increased chromatin accessibility in ovarian cancer (PMID: 39395328)
summary: LC-MS identified H1.4 as a CYP1B1-interacting protein in PARPi-resistant A2780-OlaR ovarian cancer cells. H1.4 downregulation was associated with increased chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) and higher cell viability after Olaparib, pointing to a CYP1B1/H1.4 axis in resistance.

citation: CMAHP promotes metastasis by reducing ubiquitination of Snail and inducing angiogenesis via GM-CSF overexpression in gastric cancer (PMID: 34716430)
summary: The pseudogene CMAHP interacts with histone H1.4 and promotes histone acetylation, which enhances c-Jun and RelA (p65) expression in gastric cancer cells. This drives GM-CSF transactivation and metastasis.

citation: Ablation of histone H1.4 reveals the focal regulation of AP-1 directed enhancers (PMID: 41054521)
summary: H1.4 ablation changed nascent transcription and gene expression, upregulating RAR and TNF-α/NF-κB pathways and repressing extracellular matrix and collagen genes. It caused enhancer-sized accessibility changes with concordant H3K27ac/H3K4me1 shifts, and sites that lost accessibility were enriched for the AP-1 motif.

citation: A Rahman Syndrome mutation in histone H1.4 disrupts chromatin compaction and phase separation (PMID: 42173878)
summary: Rahman syndrome frameshift mutations truncate the H1.4 C-terminal domain and reduce its positive charge. The mutant H1.4 gives more extended nucleosome arrays with more accessible linker DNA, reduced phase separation, and greater H1.4 mobility in nuclei, indicating weaker chromatin binding.

citation: Jin et al. 2025 - Genomic analysis of 11,555 probands identifies 60 dominant congenital heart disease genes (PMID: 40127276)
variant_detail: Damaging de novo mutations in LHX2 (specific variant notation not provided in the text)
phenotype: Congenital heart disease; Aortic atresia; Mitral atresia
diagnostic_reason: Significant burden of damaging de novo variants in LHX2 among CHD probands; gene pLI = 0.99; mouse knockouts produce CHD. Both probands with damaging DNMs had aortic and mitral atresia.
center_country: Pediatric Cardiac Genomics Consortium (PCGC); multicenter, likely USA

citation: Shi et al. 1997 (Porter et al.) - Lhx2, a LIM homeobox gene, is required for eye, forebrain, and definitive erythrocyte development (PMID: 9247336)
phenotype: anophthalmia: optic vesicle specified but eye development arrests before optic cup formation; cerebral cortex malformation with neocortical hypoplasia due to deficient forebrain proliferation; aplasia of hippocampal anlagen; severe anemia from a cell non-autonomous defect in definitive erythropoiesis

citation: Monuki et al. 2001 - LIM-homeodomain gene Lhx2 regulates the formation of the cortical hem (PMID: 11165475)
phenotype: expanded cortical hem covering almost the entire dorsal telencephalon at E12.5; no hippocampal differentiation adjacent to the mutant hem; overall dorsoventral patterning not perturbed; defective early telencephalic patterning

citation: Chou & Tole 2009 (Chou et al.) - Lhx2 specifies regional fate in Emx1 lineage of telencephalic progenitors generating cerebral cortex (PMID: 19820705)
phenotype: Emx1-cre deletion at E10.5 altered progenitor fate; progenitors generated three-layer cortex resembling olfactory cortex instead of lateral neocortex; no ectopic olfactory cortex after deletion at E11.5, indicating a critical period

citation: Hsu et al. 2015 - Lhx2 regulates the timing of β-catenin-dependent cortical neurogenesis (PMID: 26371318)
phenotype: Nestin-cre deletion produced a dramatically smaller cortex; reduced cortical progenitor proliferation; precocious radial glia differentiation and temporal shift of neurogenesis; Wnt/β-catenin pathway failed to maintain progenitor proliferation

citation: de Melo et al. 2016 - Lhx2 Is an Essential Factor for Retinal Gliogenesis and Notch Signaling (PMID: 26911688)
phenotype: failure of Müller glia development at all stages: reduced proliferation of gliocompetent progenitors, loss of Müller-specific gene expression, and impaired terminal differentiation; rapid downregulation of Notch pathway genes (Notch1, Dll1, Dll3, Hes1, Hes5, Sox8, Rax) and loss of Notch signaling; Hes5-induced gliogenesis requires Lhx2

citation: Subramanian et al. 2011 - Transcription factor Lhx2 is necessary and sufficient to suppress astrogliogenesis and promote neurogenesis in the developing hippocampus (PMID: 21690374)
phenotype: Lhx2 disruption by in utero electroporation and in organotypic slice culture caused premature astrocyte production in the hippocampus during the neurogenic period; loss of Lhx2 in neocortex did not cause premature astrogliogenesis

citation: Wang et al. 2017 - Lhx2 Expression in Postmitotic Cortical Neurons Initiates Assembly of the Thalamocortical Somatosensory Circuit (PMID: 28122236)
phenotype: layer 4 barrel cortex neurons initially specified but failed to form cellular barrels or polarized dendrites; thalamocortical axons reached barrel cortex but failed to arborize into barrels; downregulation of activity-regulated and barrel-formation genes including Btbd3 (direct Lhx2 target)

citation: Marcos-Mondéjar et al. 2012 - The lhx2 transcription factor controls thalamocortical axonal guidance by specific regulation of robo1 and robo2 receptors (PMID: 22457488)
phenotype: thalamus-specific Lhx2 deletion produced topographic thalamocortical axon defects, particularly in projections from the medial geniculate nucleus and caudal ventrobasal nucleus; altered Robo1 and Robo2 expression

citation: Kim et al. 2014 - Lhx2 regulates bone remodeling in mice by modulating RANKL signaling in osteoclasts (PMID: 24902903)
phenotype: osteoporotic bone phenotype; increased osteoclast formation in vivo

citation: Mardaryev et al. 2006 (Rhee et al.) - Lhx2 maintains stem cell character in hair follicles (PMID: 16809539)
phenotype: loss-of-function showed Lhx2 maintains growth and undifferentiated properties of hair follicle progenitors; hair follicle stem cell specification and maintenance defects

citation: Lhx2 specifically expressed in HSCs promotes liver regeneration and inhibits liver fibrosis (PMID: 39693275)
summary: Lhx2 is a hepatic stellate cell (HSC)-specific transcription factor that is higher in healthy than fibrotic liver in mouse and human. Knockdown impaired regeneration after acute injury. HSC-specific overexpression promoted hepatocyte proliferation and reduced fibrosis, upregulated SMAD6 to block TGF-β signaling, and acted upstream of pro-regenerative factors such as HGF.

citation: LHX2 Rewires the Metabolic and Epigenetic Landscape to Drive Tumor Progression in Prostate Cancer (PMID: 40899980)
summary: In neuroendocrine prostate cancer models, glycolysis-derived lactate and histone lactylation increase LHX2 expression. LHX2 then transcriptionally activates LDHA, forming a positive feedback loop, and upregulates DNMT1 to drive neuroendocrine gene expression and tumor growth. Paritaprevir binds LHX2 directly and suppresses neuroendocrine markers and tumor progression.

citation: Lhx2 regulates the timing of β-catenin-dependent cortical neurogenesis (PMID: 26371318)
summary: Nestin-Cre deletion of Lhx2 in cortical progenitors produced a much smaller cortex through precocious radial glia differentiation and a temporal shift in neurogenesis. Without Lhx2, Wnt/β-catenin signaling could not maintain progenitor proliferation, so Lhx2 is required for β-catenin function.

citation: Lhx2 regulates the development of the forebrain hem system (PMID: 23307637)
summary: Lhx2 limits the extent of the cortical hem, septum and thalamic eminence. Loss of Lhx2 greatly expands all three structures and dramatically increases the Cajal-Retzius cell population. Lhx2 therefore acts as a central regulator of telencephalic midline patterning.

citation: Mapping the expression of epithelial hair follicle stem cell-related transcription factors LHX2 and SOX9 in the human hair follicle (PMID: 25808706)
summary: In human anagen hair follicles, LHX2 protein is found throughout the outer root sheath, including the bulge. LHX2+ cells are mostly in the sub-bulge and proximal bulb ORS rather than restricted to the bulge. Expression increases in proximal follicle epithelium during catagen, and most SOX9+ cells do not co-express LHX2.

citation: LHX2 Mediates the FGF-to-SHH Regulatory Loop during Limb Development (PMID: 29914077)
summary: Transcriptome analysis of FGF-treated chick limb buds identified LHX2 as an intermediate in FGF-mediated regulation of SHH. LHX2 acts as a competency factor maintaining distal posterior SHH expression beneath the AER.

citation: Lhx2 regulates bone remodeling in mice by modulating RANKL signaling in osteoclasts (PMID: 24902903)
summary: Lhx2 is highly expressed in osteoclast precursors and falls during RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis. Its overexpression inhibits NFATc1 induction. Lhx2 interacts with c-Fos, reducing c-Fos DNA binding and NFATc1 transactivation. Lhx2 conditional knockout mice show an osteoporotic phenotype with increased osteoclast formation.

citation: Lhx2 mediates the activity of Six3 in zebrafish forebrain growth (PMID: 16226737)
summary: In zebrafish, the telencephalon reduction in six3a/six3b morphants was fully rescued by head-specific lhx2 overexpression (caged mRNA), whereas Six3b could not rescue lhx2 knockdown. Lhx2 acts downstream of or parallel to Six3 in controlling forebrain progenitor proliferation.

citation: MRG1 binds to the LIM domain of Lhx2 and may function as a coactivator to stimulate glycoprotein hormone alpha-subunit gene expression (PMID: 10593900)
summary: A yeast two-hybrid screen identified MRG1 as an Lhx2 LIM-domain interactor, confirmed by in vitro binding and co-immunoprecipitation in alphaT3-1 cells. The Lhx2 LIM domain has intrinsic transactivation activity, and MRG1 enhances alpha-subunit reporter activity. MRG1 also binds TBP and p300, suggesting recruitment of p300/CBP and TBP.

citation: LHX2- and LDB1-mediated trans interactions regulate olfactory receptor choice (PMID: 30626972)
summary: LHX2 binds the Greek-island enhancers in mouse olfactory sensory neurons and works with the adaptor LDB1. Together they regulate interchromosomal olfactory receptor compartments, Greek island hubs, and olfactory receptor transcription.

citation: FGF12 is a candidate Brugada syndrome locus (PMID: 24096171)
variant_detail: Q7R-FGF12 (p.Gln7Arg in FGF12-B isoform)
phenotype: Brugada syndrome; Reduced Na+ channel current density and availability in rat cardiomyocytes (functional); Reduced binding to NaV1.5 C terminus (functional)
diagnostic_reason: Single missense variant found in 102 phenotype-positive, genotype-negative BrS individuals; the mutant reduced NaV1.5 C-terminus binding, Na+ current density and availability, and action potential amplitude (loss of Na+ channel function) compared with wild-type FGF12.
center_country: USA (BrS biorepository; Mayo Clinic / Vanderbilt-affiliated investigators, not explicitly stated in abstract)

citation: De Novo FGF12 (Fibroblast Growth Factor 12) Functional Variation Is Potentially Associated With Idiopathic Ventricular Tachycardia (PMID: 28775062)
variant_detail: p.P211Q (de novo; 1.84% of 163 patients with right ventricular outflow tract VT)
phenotype: Idiopathic ventricular tachycardia; Right ventricular outflow tract VT; Downregulated FGF12 expression on western blot (functional)
diagnostic_reason: De novo variant; significantly downregulated FGF12 expression by western blotting; identified among 5 rare variants on resequencing of 320 unrelated idiopathic VT patients. The common SNP rs1460922 was also associated with VT. Only p.P211Q is described as functional.

citation: Copy number variants in Ebstein anomaly (PMID: 29216221)
variant_detail: CNV overlapping or near FGF12 (details not given in abstract)
phenotype: Ebstein anomaly
diagnostic_reason: CNV overlapped or was close to FGF12, a gene involved in early myocardial development, in a population-based cohort of 60 EA cases; prioritized as a candidate on the basis of gene content.

citation: ASHG 2017 - Copy number reanalysis: The hidden contribution of MED13L to intellectual disability
variant_detail: Likely pathogenic duplication of FGF12 (CNV detected by exome sequencing and array)
phenotype: Phenotype not specified (patient from an exome sequencing cohort of 160 probands, likely neurodevelopmental/intellectual disability)
diagnostic_reason: Classified as a likely pathogenic duplication of FGF12 in an exome sequencing CNV-calling validation against clinical SNP microarray.

citation: Fgf12 knockout mouse - Fibroblast growth factor 12 is expressed in spiral and vestibular ganglia and necessary for auditory and equilibrium function (PMID: 30065296)
phenotype: Increased hearing threshold measured by auditory brainstem response; Impaired rotarod performance; Impaired balance beam performance (equilibrium deficit); Inner ear morphology not significantly different from wild-type

citation: Macrophage-specific FGF12 promotes liver fibrosis progression in mice (PMID: 35753047)
phenotype: Myeloid-specific Fgf12 deletion protected against BDL-induced and CCl4-induced liver fibrosis; Decreased Ly6C-high macrophage population in fibrotic liver; Reduced expression of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines; Reduced hepatic stellate cell activation via MCP-1/CCR2 axis; JAK-STAT-mediated macrophage activation

citation: Loss of macrophage fibroblast growth factor 12 attenuates cardiac fibrosis in pressure-overloaded myocardium (PMID: 40188526)
phenotype: Myeloid-specific Fgf12 knockout markedly attenuated pressure overload-induced myocardial fibrosis; Altered IL-4-stimulated M2 polarization of BMDMs via SOCS/STAT pathway; Reduced ROS accumulation and activation of cardiac fibroblasts by conditioned medium from FGF12-knockdown macrophages

citation: Phenotyping of FGF12A(V52H) mutation in mouse implies a complex FGF12 network (PMID: 39142611)
phenotype: Seizure susceptibility without spontaneous seizures; Increased excitability of dorsal hippocampal CA3 neurons; Perturbed excitatory/inhibitory neuron balance in hippocampus (increased SOM+ and CaMKII+ neurons); Cognitive deficit; Impaired risk assessment behavior; Altered social behavior

citation: Depletion of Fibroblast Growth Factor 12 Restrains the Viability, Stemness, and Motility of Colorectal Cancer (PMID: 35860801)
phenotype: shFGF12 in colorectal cancer cells (LoVo, SW480) inhibited tumor growth in xenograft mouse model; Reduced EMT, cancer stemness and PI3K/AKT pathway activity in xenografts

citation: Macrophage-specific FGF12 promotes liver fibrosis progression in mice (PMID: 35753047)
summary: FGF12 is up-regulated in hepatic macrophages in BDL- and CCl4-induced fibrosis, and its levels correlate with fibrosis severity in human liver. Myeloid-specific Fgf12 knockout protected against fibrosis and reduced Ly6C-high macrophages and proinflammatory cytokines. FGF12 promotes macrophage proinflammatory activation via the JAK-STAT pathway and drives HSC activation through the MCP-1/CCR2 axis.

citation: FGF12 Positively Regulates Keratinocyte Proliferation by Stabilizing MDM2 and Inhibiting p53 Activity in Psoriasis (PMID: 39234815)
summary: FGF12 is highly expressed in psoriatic epidermis and in IMQ-induced psoriasis-like skin. FGF12 binds the RING domain of MDM2, partially blocking β-Trcp binding and K48 ubiquitination, which stabilizes MDM2 and suppresses p53 signaling. Keratinocyte-specific FGF12 loss reduced proliferation and psoriasis-like symptoms, and p53 knockdown reversed this effect.

citation: FGF12 is a novel component of the nucleolar NOLC1/TCOF1 ribosome biogenesis complex (PMID: 36411431)
summary: FGF12 localizes to the nucleolus and interacts with NOLC1 and TCOF1. The NOLC1 interaction is unique to FGF12, while other FHFs bind only TCOF1. Complex formation is phosphorylation-dependent and requires the FGF12 C-terminus. NOLC1 and TCOF1 cannot interact without FGF12, suggesting a role in ribosome biogenesis.

citation: Hair Growth Regulation by Fibroblast Growth Factor 12 (FGF12) (PMID: 36012732)
summary: FGF12 is mainly expressed in outer root sheath cells, with high expression in the anagen phase. siRNA knockdown delayed telogen-to-anagen transition in mice and reduced ORS cell proliferation and migration. Overexpression promoted migration and anagen induction, and altered expression of PDGF-CC, MDK and HB-EGF.

citation: Biallelic structural variations within FGF12 detected by long-read sequencing in epilepsy (PMID: 37286232)
summary: Biallelic intragenic SVs and a homozygous SNV in FGF12 were found in DEE patients. Expression analysis in patient lymphoblastoid cells and Drosophila in vivo functional assays of the SNV confirmed loss-of-function. This contrasts with the known heterozygous gain-of-function missense variants and duplications.

citation: Exome sequencing identified FGF12 as a novel candidate gene for Kashin-Beck disease (PMID: 26290467)
sample_size: 90 KBD patients, 1627 controls (plus 1 sib pair for exome sequencing)
summary: Exome sequencing of a KBD sib pair found a novel 3'UTR +106T>C variant in FGF12. In a GWAS, nine FGF12 SNPs showed association with KBD, the strongest being rs1847340.

citation: FGF12 is a candidate Brugada syndrome locus (PMID: 24096171)
summary: FGF12 is the major FHF expressed in human ventricle. The BrS-associated Q7R-FGF12 mutant reduced binding to the NaV1.5 C-terminus but not to junctophilin-2. In rat cardiomyocytes it reduced Na+ current density and action potential amplitude without affecting Ca2+ channels, showing that FHF effects on Na+ and Ca2+ channels are separable.

citation: Early onset epilepsy and SUDEP with cardiac arrhythmia in mice carrying the EIEE47 gain-of-function FHF1(FGF12) missense mutation (PMID: 33982289)
summary: Fhf1 R52H/+ knock-in mice show fully penetrant seizures and SUDEP with bradycardia between 12 and 26 days of age. The mutant FHF1B protein shifted cardiac sodium channel steady-state inactivation by about 15 mV depolarizing and slowed inactivation. The authors propose an FHF1/Nav1.6 functional axis in epileptic encephalopathy.

citation: FGF12 restrains mitochondria-dependent ferroptosis in doxorubicin-induced cardiomyocytes through the activation of FGFR1/AMPK/NRF2 signaling (PMID: 38349269)
summary: FGF12 is down-regulated in DOX-injured mouse myocardium. Overexpression reduced injury markers, ROS and ferroptosis markers (ACSL4, PTGS2) and increased GPX4 and FTH1. FGF12 activates FGFR1/AMPK/NRF2 signaling, and FGFR1 silencing reversed its protective effects.

citation: FGF12 Alleviates Cardiac Hypertrophy by Inhibiting Phosphorylation of CaM/CaMKII/CREB1 Axis (PMID: 41979475)
summary: FGF12 expression is reduced, and its subcellular localization altered, in HCM patient myocardium. FGF12 binds calmodulin and suppresses CaMKII/ERK1/2/CREB1/MCU phosphorylation and expression. Nuclear FGF12 binds the CREB1 promoter, lowering mitochondrial Ca2+ and ROS. AAV9-FGF12 reduced hypertrophy in HCM mouse and iPSC-cardiomyocyte models.

citation: Genomic analysis of 11,555 probands identifies 60 dominant congenital heart disease genes (PMID: 40127276)
variant_detail: Not specified in the abstract or the available full-text passage; damaging heterozygous variants (de novo and rare transmitted/unphased) in KLF2 were significantly enriched in CHD probands
phenotype: Congenital heart disease (association with a single cardiac phenotype; specific subtype not stated in the excerpt)
diagnostic_reason: Significant burden of damaging heterozygous variants (de novo and rare transmitted) in KLF2 among CHD probands after multiple-comparison adjustment. KLF2 was among the 33 genes significantly associated with a single cardiac phenotype (Table 1).

citation: Tang et al. 2021 - KLF2 regulates neutrophil activation and thrombosis in cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure progression (PMID: 34793333)
phenotype: Neutrophil-specific Klf2 loss promotes neutrophil activation and NETosis in the angiotensin II model; Sporadic thrombosis in small myocardial vessels; Myocardial hypoxia, cell death and cardiac hypertrophy; Cardiac dysfunction and heart failure progression; Reduced Klf2 expression in leukocytes of the rodent heart failure model; Crosstalk with HIF1 signaling

citation: Chronic NK cell activation results in a dysfunctional, tissue resident-like state mediated by KLF2 deficiency (PMID: 40857665)
phenotype: Conditional KLF2 deficiency in NK cells (mixed bone marrow chimeras) causes altered homing; NK cells acquire tissue resident-like features in vivo; KLF2 loss/gain-of-function affects NK cytotoxicity, cytokine production and chemotaxis

citation: Neutrophil KLF2 regulates inflammasome-dependent neonatal mortality from endotoxemia (PMID: 40170486)
phenotype: Myeloid-Klf2 deletion decreases survival after endotoxemia in a developmentally dependent manner, with higher mortality at P4 than at P12; Increased proinflammatory cytokines, notably IL-1β, in P4 knockout pups; Greater NLRP3 inflammasome priming and activation and IL-1β release by bone marrow neutrophils; Survival rescued by neutrophil depletion or NLRP3 inhibition (MCC950); Enrichment of proinflammatory pathways in knockout neutrophils

citation: KLF2 maintains lineage fidelity and suppresses CD8 T cell exhaustion during acute LCMV infection (PMID: 39946463)
phenotype: In vivo CRISPR-Cas9 knockout of Klf2 in CD8 T cells causes aberrant differentiation to exhausted-like cells during acute LCMV infection; Loss of suppression of TOX; Impaired TBET-driven effector differentiation; Loss of the polyfunctional tumor-specific progenitor state

citation: Lymph nodes fuel KLF2-dependent effector CD8(+) T cell differentiation during chronic infection and checkpoint blockade (PMID: 40954251)
phenotype: CD62L+ TPEX and CX3CR1+ TEX developmental lineage depends on KLF2; KLF2 dependence of effector-like exhausted T cell differentiation in lymph nodes during chronic LCMV infection and checkpoint blockade

citation: Piezo1-Regulated Mechanotransduction Controls Flow-Activated Lymphatic Expansion (PMID: 35701867)
phenotype: Lymphatic-specific Piezo1 knockout phenocopies the sprouting defects of Orai1- or Klf2-knockout lymphatics during embryo development (Klf2 knockout lymphatic sprouting defects referenced; Klf2 is a downstream target); Postnatal Piezo1 deletion causes lymphatic regression in adults

citation: Zebrafish Congenital Heart Disease Models: Opportunities and Challenges (PMID: 38892128)
phenotype: klf2a mutant: atrioventricular valve defects, valvular hypoplasia and absence of leaflets (review table)

citation: 2022 - A mitochondrial contribution to anti-inflammatory shear stress signaling in vascular endothelial cells (PMID: 35695893)
summary: A whole-genome CRISPR-Cas9 screen for genes required for laminar shear stress induction of Klf2 found that induction requires the MEKK2/3-MEK5-ERK5 kinase module plus mitochondrial calcium/ROS signaling and a mitophagy/p62 scaffold. Blocking the mitochondrial pathway in vivo reduced KLF2-dependent genes such as eNOS, and Klf2 expression was limited in regions of disturbed flow.

citation: 2025 - Endothelial SRSF1 Promotes Ischemia-Induced Angiogenesis via ATF3-KLF2-S1PR1 Pathway (PMID: 41195527)
summary: Full-length ATF3, whose splicing is promoted by SRSF1, binds directly to the KLF2 promoter and suppresses KLF2 expression and downstream S1PR1 signaling. This KLF2 suppression enhances endothelial tube formation and angiogenesis after hindlimb ischemia.

citation: 2021 - KLF2 regulates neutrophil activation and thrombosis in cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure progression (PMID: 34793333)
summary: Klf2 mRNA is markedly reduced in leukocytes from human heart failure subjects and a rodent heart failure model. In mice, angiotensin II activates a neutrophil KLF2/NETosis pathway, partly through crosstalk with HIF1 signaling, which drives microvascular thrombosis, myocardial hypoxia and hypertrophy.

citation: 2024 - N6-methyladenosine modification of KLF2 may contribute to endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition in pulmonary hypertension (PMID: 38741032)
summary: METTL3-mediated m6A modification of KLF2 mRNA maintains KLF2 expression, and mutating the m6A site compromises it. KLF2 overexpression restores CD31 and VE-cadherin, reduces SM22, N-cadherin and EndMT transcription factors, and directly binds the SM22 promoter, so it protects against EndMT in pulmonary hypertension.

citation: 2020 - Therapeutic potential of KLF2-induced exosomal microRNAs in pulmonary hypertension (PMID: 32132543)
summary: KLF2 induces exosomal miR-181a-5p and miR-324-5p, which target Notch4 and ETS1 to attenuate pulmonary vascular remodelling. KLF2 and these miRNAs are reduced in pre-clinical, idiopathic and heritable PAH, including a case with the missense p.H288Y KLF2 mutation, and miRNA supplementation attenuates disease in PAH mice.

citation: 2016 - Dendritic Cell KLF2 Expression Regulates T Cell Activation and Proatherogenic Immune Responses (PMID: 27837103)
summary: CD11c-cre conditional Klf2 knockout in dendritic cells increased CD40 and CD86 costimulatory molecule expression and T cell proliferation and apoptosis. Transplanting bone marrow from these mice into Ldlr-/- mice aggravated atherosclerosis, showing that KLF2 restrains DC activation and proatherogenic T cell responses.

citation: 2017 - Regulation of endothelial hemoglobin alpha expression by Kruppel-like factors (PMID: 28825355)
summary: KLF2 and KLF4 gain of function induces HBA in endothelial cells, and endothelial Klf2/Klf4 knockout has the opposite effect. KLF2/KLF4 transactivate the hemoglobin alpha promoter through KLF-binding sites 2, 3 and 4, and ChIP showed KLF4 binding to the promoter.

citation: 2024 - Epigenetic regulation by polycomb repressive complex 1 promotes cerebral cavernous malformations (PMID: 39402138)
summary: Loss of CCM1/CCM2/CCM3 triggers a MAPK-KLF2 signaling cascade. The PRC1 component CBX7 contributes to pathological KLF2 signaling and to activation of KLF2 target genes including TEK, ANGPT1, WNT9 and endoMT genes, and its silencing or inhibition suppresses CCM phenotypes in zebrafish, HUVECs and a murine CCM3 model.

citation: 2021 - G protein-coupled estrogen receptor regulates the KLF2-dependent eNOS expression by activating of Ca(2+) and EGFR signaling pathway in human endothelial cells (PMID: 34363795)
summary: The GPER agonist G-1 increased KLF2 and eNOS expression in EA.hy926 cells and HUVECs through Gαq/Gβγ, Ca2+/CaMKKβ/AMPK/CaMKIIα-HDAC5 and Src/EGFR/ERK5/MEF2C signaling. Silencing KLF2 or GPER attenuated the G-1-induced eNOS expression.

citation: 2013 - Aβ(1-42) disrupts the expression and function of KLF2 in Alzheimer's disease mediated by p53 (PMID: 23313511)
summary: KLF2 expression is decreased in the brains of Tg2576 AD mice because of Aβ accumulation. KLF2 overexpression fully rescued Aβ(1-42)-induced loss of Occludin in human brain endothelial cells (HBMECs), and p53 mediated the Aβ-induced KLF2 reduction.

citation: 2016 - Cross-talk between autophagy and KLF2 determines endothelial cell phenotype and microvascular function in acute liver injury (PMID: 27545498)
summary: KLF2 inducers (statins, resveratrol, shear stress, KLF2 adenovirus) raise endothelial KLF2 through a Rac1-Rab7-autophagy dependent mechanism, and KLF2 in turn activates autophagy, forming a positive feedback loop. Simvastatin maintained autophagy and KLF2 after cold ischemia/reperfusion and improved microvascular function in liver injury.

citation: ASHG 2016 - Partial trisomy 5q and partial monosomy 13q result in developmental delay with characteristic facial features. (L. Dupuis, M. Shago, R. Mendoza-Londono)
variant_detail: Terminal deletion of 13q34 (~1.765 Mb, 33 RefSeq genes including CHAMP1) from a paternal t(5;13)(q33.3;q34), with concurrent 23.2 Mb duplication of 5q33.3-qter
phenotype: developmental delay (moderate, mainly language and fine motor); hypertelorism; flat midface; thin upper lip with long simple philtrum; low-set posteriorly rotated ears; small mouth; small patent foramen ovale
diagnostic_reason: Unbalanced derivative of a paternal balanced translocation, detected by genomic microarray. The phenotype is attributed mainly to the distal 5q trisomy. CHAMP1 is only one of several genes lost in the 13q34 deletion, so its individual contribution is unclear.
center_country: Hospital for Sick Children, Toronto, Canada (presumed from the authors; not explicitly stated)

citation: Mutations in genes related to myocyte contraction and ventricular septum development in non-syndromic tetralogy of Fallot (PMID: 37840956)
variant_detail: chr13:114324530 C>T, p.Gln230* (stop gained)
phenotype: non-syndromic tetralogy of Fallot
diagnostic_reason: Rare de novo stop-gained variant identified by trio exome sequencing and predicted high impact (listed among 120 likely deleterious variants). CHAMP1 is annotated to autism/intellectual disability and cytoskeleton organization.

citation: Genomic testing and molecular diagnosis among infants with congenital heart disease in the neonatal intensive care unit (PMID: 38499751)
variant_detail: Single nucleotide variant in CHAMP1 (specific change not given in the available text)
phenotype: congenital heart disease; NICU admission with suspicion of a genetic disorder
diagnostic_reason: Molecular diagnosis from genetic testing (exome or gene panel) in an infant with CHD. No variant-level detail is given.
center_country: Boston Children's Hospital and Children's Memorial Hermann Hospital (Houston), USA

citation: Identifying phenotypic expansions for congenital diaphragmatic hernia plus (CDH+) using DECIPHER data (PMID: 35904974)
phenotype: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia plus (CDH+) with additional birth defects; Mental retardation, autosomal dominant 40 (MIM 616579) as the associated disorder
diagnostic_reason: Classified as pathogenic frameshift variant in a CDH+ individual (Subject 2) from the DECIPHER database; the gene is associated with autosomal dominant MRD40. The table lists a 81% value, which probably reflects a predicted score from a CDH machine-learning model. Inheritance is not stated in the excerpt.

citation: Deficiency of CHAMP1, a gene related to intellectual disability, causes impaired neuronal development and a mild behavioural phenotype (PMID: 36106092)
phenotype: Homozygous KO mice slightly smaller than wild-type; Homozygous KO mice died soon after birth on pure C57BL/6J background; No gross anatomical brain defects in CHAMP1-/- mice; Increased mitotic cells in cerebral cortex; Delayed neuronal differentiation in CHAMP1-/- neural stem cells in vitro, also suggested in vivo by CHAMP1 knockdown; Heterozygous KO adults showed mild memory defects, altered social interaction, and depression-like behaviours; Downregulation of genes related to neurotransmitter transport and neurodevelopmental disorder in embryonic CHAMP1-/- brains
knockout_type: full knockout (homozygous) and heterozygous knockout; also in vivo knockdown

citation: ASHG 2023 - Characterization of a novel mouse model with 35 bp deletion in Champ1 gene and exploration of AAV gene therapy to correct phenotypic consequences arising from CHAMP1 mutations
phenotype: Delay in motor development; Impairment in memory and learning abilities
knockout_type: other (CRISPR/Cas9 35 bp deletion in exon 2; heterozygous breeding, likely loss-of-function)
sample_size: 20 mice per battery (4 cohorts total, 2 cohorts per battery)

citation: ASHG 2022 - Characterization of novel mouse model with 35 bp deletion in Champ1 gene and exploration of AAV gene therapy to correct syndromes arising from mutations in the CHAMP1
phenotype: Females presented difficulty giving birth due to dystocia

citation: Tomida et al. 2022 - CHAMP1-POGZ counteracts the inhibitory effect of 53BP1 on homologous recombination and affects PARP inhibitor resistance (PMID: 35393543)
summary: CHAMP1 is recruited to laser-induced DSB sites and, together with POGZ, promotes HR through DNA end resection (pRPA2 and CtIP recruitment) but not NHEJ. CHAMP1 depletion reduced BRCA1 recruitment but not 53BP1 recruitment. Loss of CHAMP1 or POGZ restored PARP inhibitor sensitivity in cells depleted of both 53BP1 and BRCA1.

citation: CHAMP1 binds to REV7/FANCV and promotes homologous recombination repair (PMID: 36044844)
summary: CHAMP1 binds directly to the REV7 seatbelt domain and reduces Shieldin complex levels, which increases DSB end resection and promotes HR. It also interacts with POGZ in a heterochromatin complex. CHAMP1 overexpression in human tumors promotes HR, confers PARP inhibitor resistance, and correlates with poor prognosis.

citation: Structural basis for MAD2L2 (REV7) interaction with CAMP/CHAMP1 (PMID: 28887307)
summary: Crystal structures of human MAD2L2 in complex with a CHAMP1 (CAMP) fragment show a binding mode similar to MAD2L2-REV3 but with different residue interactions. The interaction depends on the WK motif of CHAMP1. In one crystal form the complex dimerized with a swapped MAD2L2 C-terminal region.

citation: CHAMP1 complex directs heterochromatin assembly and promotes homology-directed DNA repair (PMID: 39962076)
summary: The CHAMP1-POGZ-HP1α complex recruits SETDB1 and promotes heterochromatin assembly at centromeres, telomeres, and ALT telomeres, and enhances HDR in these regions. Peripheral blood lymphocytes from CHAMP1 syndrome patients show defective heterochromatin clustering and DSB repair.

citation: CHAMP1 complex promotes heterochromatin assembly and reduces replication stress (PMID: 41481470)
summary: The CHAMP1 complex is transiently recruited to stalled replication forks, where it deposits H3K9me3, stabilizes forks, and protects them from MRE11 degradation. CHAMP1 loss increases micronuclei and compensatory FA and ATR/CHK1 pathway activity. CHAMP1 deficiency is synthetic lethal with FANCM inhibition in ALT tumor cells, and the complex is essential for survival of CCNE1-amplified ovarian cancer.

citation: CHAMP1 PTC mutations cause a homologous recombination defect through haploinsufficiency (PMID: 39738383)
summary: Patient LCLs and fibroblasts with CHAMP1 PTC mutations express truncated proteins, and the fibroblasts have an HR defect. The PTC mutants could not restore HR when endogenous CHAMP1 was depleted, whereas missense mutants could. Heterozygous CHAMP1 depletion in DLD-1 cells caused an HR defect, indicating haploinsufficiency.

citation: CHAMP1 is an essential regulator for human myoblast fusion and muscle development (PMID: 41540007)
summary: CHAMP1 acts as a MyoD cofactor that directly activates expression of the fusogen Myomaker, and is needed for human myoblast fusion in vitro and in vivo. Patient-derived cells show fusion defects that Myomaker restoration fully rescues. The C2H2 zinc-finger motifs of CHAMP1 are necessary and sufficient for MyoD interaction and Myomaker expression.

citation: Chromosome alignment-maintaining phosphoprotein CHAMP1 plays a role in cell survival through regulating Mcl-1 expression (PMID: 34107118)
summary: CHAMP1 depletion accelerates mitotic cell death after mitotic arrest and reduces anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family proteins, especially Mcl-1. CHAMP1 maintains Mcl-1 mRNA and protein, stabilizing the protein by suppressing proteasomal degradation. Depletion reduces cell viability and acts synergistically with antimitotic drugs.

citation: Characterization of Electrophysiological and Transcriptomic Alterations in Patient-Derived Neurons from CHAMP1 Syndrome (PMID: 42395457)
sample_size: two patient iPSC lines with different CHAMP1 mutations
summary: Patient iPSC-derived NPCs and excitatory neurons carrying two CHAMP1 mutations show dosage-dependent reduced proliferation and allele-specific DNA repair/HR dysfunction. Mutant neurons have depolarized resting potential, reduced firing, reduced Na+/K+ currents, impaired neurite outgrowth, and altered synaptic activity. Single-nucleus RNA-seq shows delayed developmental trajectories and dysregulated synaptic genes enriched for autism, ADHD, and epilepsy risk genes.

citation: ASHG 2023 - Characterization of a novel mouse model with 35 bp deletion in Champ1 gene and exploration of AAV gene therapy (T. Carneiro et al.)
sample_size: 4 cohorts; 2 cohorts (20 mice) per behavioral battery
summary: A CRISPR/Cas9 35 bp deletion in Champ1 exon 2 in C57BL/6NCrl mice produced heterozygous mice with delayed motor development and impaired learning and memory. An AAV9 vector carrying wild-type CHAMP1 is planned to rescue the phenotype.

citation: Lang et al. 2006 - Cranio-lenticulo-sutural dysplasia is caused by a SEC23A mutation leading to abnormal endoplasmic-reticulum-to-Golgi trafficking (PMID: 16980979)
phenotype: sec23a morpholino-injected embryos show a phenotype reminiscent of CLSD; craniofacial/skeletal morphogenesis defects
