citation: Sarmah et al. 2010 - Secretory COPII coat component Sec23a is essential for craniofacial chondrocyte maturation (PMID: 16980978)
phenotype: crusher mutant (sec23a L402X nonsense) with malformed craniofacial skeleton; kinked pectoral fins; short body length; normal development until onset of craniofacial chondrogenesis; chondrocytes accumulate protein in a distended ER; severe reduction of cartilage ECM including type II collagen; sec23b also required for ECM secretion in chondrocytes; COPI knockdown does not impair craniofacial morphogenesis

citation: Zebrafish sec23a mutant lymphangiogenesis study - Localised Collagen2a1 secretion supports lymphatic endothelial cell migration in the zebrafish embryo (PMID: 32839180)
phenotype: sec23a mutant LECs leave the cardinal vein but fail to continue migrating; failed developmental lymphangiogenesis; Col2a1 (type II collagen) secretion from notochord sheath cells fails in the mutant; blood vessel/lymphatic vascular defects

citation: Zebrafish CLSD model O-GlcNAcylation study - Dynamic Glycosylation Governs the Vertebrate COPII Protein Trafficking Pathway (PMID: 29161034)
phenotype: sec23a loss in the zebrafish CLSD model impairs collagen trafficking and skeletogenesis; rescue with wild-type SEC23A, but not with SEC23A O-GlcNAc site mutants; craniofacial/skeletal defects

citation: Functions of the COPII gene paralogs SEC23A and SEC23B are interchangeable in vivo (PMID: 30065114)
phenotype: Sec23a coding sequence inserted into the murine Sec23b locus fully rescues the lethal SEC23B-deficient pancreatic phenotype; a sec23a-expressing transgene rescues the lethality of zebrafish sec23b deficiency

citation: Saito et al. 2009 - Regulation of endoplasmic reticulum stress response by a BBF2H7-mediated Sec23a pathway is essential for chondrogenesis (PMID: 19767744)
phenotype: Bbf2h7-/- (upstream regulator of Sec23a) mice show severe chondrodysplasia; death by suffocation shortly after birth due to an immature chest cavity; loss of columnar structure in the proliferating zone; reduced hypertrophic zone; expanded ER in chondrocytes with aggregated Col2 and COMP; restored matrix protein secretion when Sec23a was reintroduced

citation: Zebrafish feelgood mutant study - The feelgood mutation in zebrafish dysregulates COPII-dependent secretion of select extracellular matrix proteins in skeletal morphogenesis (PMID: 21729877)
phenotype: creb3l2 hypomorphic mutant (regulator of sec23a/sec23b/sec24d expression) with malformed head skeleton; shortened body length; collagen II and IV backlog in rough ER; impaired collagen deposition in the ECM

citation: Lu et al. 2006 - Secretory COPII coat component Sec23a is essential for craniofacial chondrocyte maturation (PMID: 16980978)
summary: Zebrafish crusher mutant carries a sec23a nonsense mutation (L402X). Mutant chondrocytes accumulate proteins in a distended ER, with severely reduced cartilage ECM and type II collagen. sec23b is also needed for ECM secretion in chondrocytes. This is a vertebrate model of the human SEC23A-linked cranio-lenticulo-sutural dysplasia.

citation: Functions of the COPII gene paralogs SEC23A and SEC23B are interchangeable in vivo (PMID: 30065114)
summary: Human SEC23A and SEC23B have indistinguishable interactomes. Both human and murine SEC23A/B complement yeast Sec23. A sec23a transgene rescues sec23b-deficient zebrafish, and Sec23a inserted into the murine Sec23b locus rescues the SEC23B-deficient pancreatic phenotype. SEC23A is the predominant paralog in mouse bone marrow's reciprocal pattern, i.e. SEC23B is dominant in human marrow but not mouse, while the pancreas shows the reverse. Phenotypic differences are therefore attributed to expression shifts.

citation: SEC23A rescues SEC23B-deficient congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type II (PMID: 34818036)
summary: SEC23A expressed from the Sec23b locus rescues the SEC23B-deficient mouse phenotype. Erythroid deletion of all four Sec23 alleles is embryonic lethal with CDAII features. In SEC23B-deficient HUDEP-2 cells, features of CDAII were rescued by increased SEC23A expression, suggesting a therapeutic strategy.

citation: Zhou et al. 2017 - ULK1 phosphorylates Sec23A and mediates autophagy-induced inhibition of ER-to-Golgi traffic (PMID: 28486929)
summary: ULK1 phosphorylates Sec23A at S207, S312 and T405. Phosphorylation reduces Sec23A-Sec31A interaction, causes ERES aggregation and inhibits ER-to-Golgi cargo transport during autophagy induction. S207 phospho-mutants best recapitulate these effects.

citation: Identification of Cysteine Ubiquitylation Sites on the Sec23A Protein of the COPII Complex Required for Vesicle Formation from the ER (PMID: 28553408)
summary: Sec23a is mono-ubiquitylated on cysteines 432 and 449 rather than lysines, and this does not drive its degradation. Ubiquitylation appears to modulate Sec23a interaction with the ER membrane and thereby COPII formation.

citation: CREB3L2-mediated expression of Sec23A/Sec24D is involved in hepatic stellate cell activation through ER-Golgi transport (PMID: 28801610)
summary: Sec23A and Sec24D are specifically upregulated during hepatic stellate cell activation, driven by the transcription factor CREB3L2/BBF2H7. Knockdown of these components abrogated HSC activation, so Sec23A-mediated ER-to-Golgi trafficking is required.

citation: Downregulation of Sec23A protein by miRNA-375 in prostate carcinoma (PMID: 21593139)
summary: The SEC23A 3'-UTR is a target of miR-375 and miR-200c, and both downregulate Sec23A in 293T cells. SEC23A mRNA correlates inversely with miR-375 in primary prostate cancer, and Sec23A protein is decreased in tumor tissue and in LNCaP/DU145 cells. Sec23A overexpression reduced growth without inducing apoptosis, while its inhibition stimulated proliferation.

citation: Korpal et al. 2011 - Direct targeting of Sec23a by miR-200s influences cancer cell secretome and promotes metastatic colonization (PMID: 21822286)
summary: miR-200s directly target Sec23a in breast cancer cells. This reduces secretion of metastasis-suppressive proteins (Igfbp4, Tinagl1) and promotes metastatic colonization in mouse models.

citation: Conserved exchange of paralog proteins during neuronal differentiation (PMID: 35273078)
summary: A SEC23A-to-SEC23B paralog substitution occurs during neuronal differentiation and is conserved across fish, rodents and humans. RNAi altering the SEC23A/SEC23B ratio is sufficient to influence neuron differentiation.

citation: ASHG 2010 - A novel SEC23A missense mutation causing Cranio-Lenticulo-Sutural Dysplasia is involved in the MAPK signaling pathway
summary: Patient fibroblasts with SEC23A M702V showed a collagen secretion defect and enlarged ER. They also had decreased MAPK/Erk phosphorylation and cyclin D1, increased AKT phosphorylation, and G0/G1 arrest. Transfection of wild-type fibroblasts with the 702V plasmid reproduced the reduced Erk and cyclin D1.

citation: Variants in NR6A1 cause a novel oculo vertebral renal syndrome (PMID: 40610405)
phenotype: Knockdown of either or both zebrafish paralogs (nr6a1a/nr6a1b) causes abnormal eye development (coloboma/microphthalmia-related); Abnormal kidney development; Abnormal somite development; Phenotypes rescued by wild-type but not variant NR6A1 mRNA, supporting pathogenicity of patient variants

citation: Variants in NR6A1 cause a novel oculo-vertebral-renal (OVR) syndrome (PMID: 39606449)
phenotype: Knockdown of either or both zebrafish NR6A1 paralogs causes abnormal eye development; Abnormal somite development; Rescued by wild-type but not variant NR6A1 mRNA

citation: Variants in NR6A1 as a cause for congenital renal, vertebral and uterine anomalies (PMID: 41733738)
phenotype: CRISPR-Cas9 mutants for nr6a1a and nr6a1b recapitulate human phenotype; Impaired kidney development with pronephros segmentation defects; Adult kidney hypoplasia; Axial skeletal abnormalities; Cloacal anomalies; Disrupted anteroposterior expression of posterior hox genes

citation: NR6A1 is essential for neural crest cell specification, formation and survival (PMID: 41611698)
phenotype: Loss of function perturbs anterior cranial neural crest cell formation and survival; Complete agenesis of migratory neural crest cells caudal to the first pharyngeal arch; Perturbed NCC specification and epithelial-mesenchymal transition; Persistent expression of pluripotency-associated factors (e.g., Oct4); Conditional temporal deletion shows Nr6a1 required during mid-late gastrulation; Wnt1-Cre unsuitable for studying NCC specification
knockout_type: full knockout and conditional knockout (temporal deletion)

citation: Revisiting the role of GCNF in embryonic development (PMID: 24029702)
phenotype: GCNF knockout embryos die around E10.5; Failure to restrict Oct4 expression to primordial germ cells after gastrulation

citation: The function of Xenopus germ cell nuclear factor (xGCNF) in morphogenetic movements during neurulation (PMID: 12729562)
phenotype: Morpholino knockdown of xEmGCNF causes defects from neurulation onward; Defective neural tube formation; Short and curved main body axis; Impaired cell intercalation in Keller sandwich explants; Abnormal fibronectin distribution; Reduced integrin alpha5 and alpha6 expression

citation: The germ cell nuclear factor is required for retinoic acid signaling during Xenopus development (PMID: 12676320)
phenotype: Morpholino knockdown of xEmGCNF blocks the effect of RA on primary neurogenesis; Derepression of CYP26; Altered hindbrain patterning resembling reduced RA signaling; Reduced RAR gamma expression in presumptive hindbrain

citation: Anteroposterior patterning and organogenesis of Xenopus laevis require a correct dose of germ cell nuclear factor (xGCNF) (PMID: 10349627)
phenotype: Dominant-negative GCNF interfered with neural tube differentiation; Affected anterior structures including cement gland and eyes; Early gastrulation and neurulation and mesodermal markers normal; Selective anterior suppression of xRAR gamma 2; Rescued by co-expression of full-length GCNF; Overexpression caused posterior defects and disturbed somite formation

citation: Orphan nuclear receptor function in the ovary (PMID: 17485308)
phenotype: Conditional GCNF knockout used to bypass embryonic lethality of null mice to uncover roles of GCNF in the oocyte; Null mice are embryonic lethal

citation: Nr6a1 controls Hox expression dynamics and is a master regulator of vertebrate trunk development (PMID: 36522318)
summary: In mouse, Nr6a1 controls vertebral number and trunk segmentation independently of the tail region. It is needed for timely progression of Hox signatures and for the neural versus mesodermal fate choice in axial progenitors, so changes in Nr6a1 levels may underlie evolutionary changes in axial formulae.

citation: Variants in NR6A1 cause a novel oculo vertebral renal syndrome (PMID: 40610405)
summary: Six rare NR6A1 variants were found by genome sequencing in six families with autosomal dominant oculo-vertebral-renal syndrome (colobomatous microphthalmia, missing vertebrae, kidney anomalies). Zebrafish knockdown of one or both NR6A1 paralogs caused eye, kidney and somite defects. Wild-type but not variant NR6A1 mRNA rescued these defects, supporting pathogenicity.

citation: NR6A1 is essential for neural crest cell specification, formation and survival (PMID: 41611698)
summary: Nr6a1 is expressed in mouse embryos in a pattern that overlaps early neural crest development. Its loss impairs cranial neural crest formation and survival, with agenesis of migratory neural crest caudal to the first pharyngeal arch. Pluripotency factors such as Oct4 persist and EMT and specification are disrupted. Nr6a1 is required during mid-late gastrulation, where it may act as a switch that represses pluripotency factors and activates neural crest specifiers.

citation: NR6A1 regulates lipid metabolism through mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 in HepG2 cells (PMID: 31315616)
summary: NR6A1 knockdown in HepG2 cells increased lipid accumulation, insulin-induced proliferation and migration, and expression of lipogenic genes (FAS, DGAT2, ME1, MTTP, PEPCK) and CPT1a. These effects ran through mTORC1 (not mTORC2). Knockdown also raised INSR expression and insulin-induced mTOR/AKT phosphorylation, partly via miR-205-5p.

citation: Linear ubiquitination modification of NR6A1 by LUBAC inhibits RIPK3 kinase activity and attenuates apoptosis of vascular smooth muscle cells (PMID: 35543488)
summary: NR6A1 is nuclear and its protein level rises in atherosclerotic rat aorta. It promotes VSMC apoptosis and caspase activity by inducing RIPK3 phosphorylation. LUBAC co-immunoprecipitates with NR6A1 and linearly ubiquitinates it, lowering NR6A1 levels and RIPK3 activity and reducing apoptosis.

citation: NR6A1 couples with cAMP response element binding protein and regulates vascular smooth muscle cell migration (PMID: 26546462)
summary: NR6A1 interacts with CREB, nuclear actin and RNA polymerase II large subunit in VSMCs. It binds the SPP1 promoter via a CRE site and represses SPP1 expression and CRE activity. NR6A1 overexpression inhibits PDGF-induced migration, and adenoviral NR6A1 delivery attenuated stenosis after balloon injury in rats.

citation: Positive expression of NR6A1/CT150 as a predictor of biochemical recurrence-free survival in prostate cancer patients (PMID: 28969082)
significance: Gleason P=0.003; stage P=0.042; recurrence univariate P=0.0159, multivariate P=0.0317
summary: NR6A1 protein was positive in 29.7% of 303 prostate cancers and mRNA in 28.1% of 32 cases. Expression correlated with Gleason score and tumor stage and predicted shorter biochemical recurrence-free survival. Knockdown caused G0/G1 arrest and reduced invasion and EMT in DU145 and PC3 cells; overexpression promoted invasion, EMT and tumor growth in vivo.

citation: Mitofusin 2 Mediates the Protective Effect of NR6A1 Silencing Against Neuronal Injury in Experimental Stroke Models (PMID: 39259438)
summary: NR6A1 increases in neurons in in vivo and in vitro ischemia models. NR6A1 represses MFN2 transcription, and its knockdown reduced mitochondrial dysfunction and ER stress in OGD/R HT-22 cells and reduced infarction in MCAO mice. MFN2 mediated the protective effect of NR6A1 silencing.

citation: Hippocampal NR6A1 impairs CREB-BDNF signaling and leads to the development of depression-like behaviors in mice (PMID: 35183538)
summary: NR6A1 is expressed in the nuclei of mouse brain neurons, and chronic stress raised hippocampal NR6A1 protein. NR6A1 reduced CREB phosphorylation and BDNF, and its overexpression induced depression-like behaviors. Knockdown prevented stress-induced depression-like behavior, an effect that depended on CREB and BDNF.

citation: Extra-germ cell expression of mouse nuclear receptor subfamily 6, group A, member 1 (NR6A1) (PMID: 19164181)
summary: Using an Nr6a1-LacZ knockin reporter, RT-PCR and IHC, Nr6a1 was found in gametes and also in somatic tissues: epididymal sperm, oviduct epithelium, lung bronchioles, brain regions (hippocampus, cortex, cerebellum, thalamus), pituitary, parathyroid and pancreatic islets.

citation: Loss of hepatic DRP1 exacerbates alcoholic hepatitis by inducing megamitochondria and mitochondrial maladaptation (PMID: 35698731)
phenotype: Liver-specific Drp1 KO (L-DRP1 KO) mice had increased megamitochondria; Decreased mitophagy; Increased liver injury and inflammation, further exacerbated by chronic-plus-binge alcohol feeding; Attenuated alcohol-induced increases in mitochondrial oxygen consumption, hepatic NAD+, acylcarnitine and ketones, indicating metabolic maladaptation; Increased cGAS-STING-interferon pathway gene expression regardless of alcohol; Increased cytosolic mtDNA and mitochondrial dysfunction with alcohol

citation: Mitochondrial division prevents neurodegeneration (PMID: 22732519)
phenotype: Loss of Drp1 (DNM1L) in postmitotic neurons (cre-loxP) caused increased mitochondrial oxidative damage; Impaired respiration; Neurodegeneration; Accumulation of LC3, SQSTM1/p62 and ubiquitin on division-defective mitochondria, suggesting decreased mitochondrial turnover

citation: Mitochondrial dynamics and quality control regulate proteostasis in neuronal ischemia-reperfusion (PMID: 40016670)
phenotype: Neuronal mitochondrial proteostasis response to in vitro ischemia-reperfusion (OGD/R) was influenced by fusion and fission machinery, including DNM1L/DRP1 cKO in neurons

citation: Peroxisomes control mitochondrial dynamics and the mitochondrion-dependent apoptosis pathway (PMID: 31076512)
phenotype: In Pex3- or Pex5-knockout MEFs, mitochondrial fragmentation was dependent on Drp1 (DNM1L); Peroxisome deficiency increased cytosolic cytochrome c and caspase activity and enhanced etoposide-induced apoptosis

citation: Drp1 splice variants regulate ovarian cancer mitochondrial dynamics and tumor progression (PMID: 39191946)
summary: The Drp1 (DNM1L) splice variant lacking exon 16 localizes to microtubules and associates less with mitochondrial fission sites. This produces fused mitochondrial networks, enhanced respiration, pro-tumorigenic phenotypes, impaired fission in response to apoptotic stimuli, and reduced chemosensitivity. High expression of this variant relative to other transcripts predicts poor outcome in ovarian cancer patients, and variant-specific siRNAs reverse the effects.

citation: Obesity causes mitochondrial fragmentation and dysfunction in white adipocytes due to RalA activation (PMID: 38286821)
summary: RalA activation in white adipocytes after high-fat diet reverses the inhibitory Ser637 phosphorylation of Drp1, increasing fission and mitochondrial fragmentation. Adipose tissue DNM1L expression correlates positively with obesity and insulin resistance in humans.

citation: Aberrant mitochondrial morphology and function associated with impaired mitophagy and DNM1L-MAPK/ERK signaling in aged LRRK2(R1441G) mice (PMID: 33300446)
summary: DNM1L/Drp1 knockdown in MEFs slowed mitochondrial clearance, so DNM1L is required for mitophagy, and it disrupted the mitochondrial network. FCCP-induced DNM1L-Ser616 and ERK phosphorylation occurred in WT but not LRRK2 R1441G mutant MEFs, despite similar total DNM1L levels, indicating impaired DNM1L activation in the mutant.

citation: ERK1/2-mediated activation of DRP1 regulates mitochondrial dynamics and apoptosis in chondrocytes (PMID: 34767958)
summary: DRP1 expression is elevated in human OA cartilage and in mouse DMM joints. IL-1β induces DRP1 expression and activity through ERK1/2, causing mitochondrial fragmentation and Bax-mediated cytochrome c release with apoptosis. Mdivi-1 or ERK1/2 inhibition blocks these effects.

citation: Targeting DNM1L/DRP1-FIS1 axis inhibits high-grade glioma progression by impeding mitochondrial respiratory cristae remodeling (PMID: 39350223)
sample_size: 54 resected glioma patients; 7141 mitochondria analyzed by TEM
summary: DNM1L/DRP1 positively regulates FIS1, while MFF competitively inhibits FIS1 interaction. DNM1L/DRP1-FIS1 axis knockdown impaired mitophagy, cristae remodeling and OXPHOS, and reduced proliferation and xenograft growth of glioma cells and stem cells.

citation: Cancer-associated SNRPD3 mutation confers resistance to hypoxia, which is attenuated by DRP1 inhibition (PMID: 38241813)
summary: The SNRPD3 G96V spliceosome mutation causes differential splicing of DNM1L mRNA under hypoxia and excessive mitochondrial fragmentation. The DRP1 inhibitor Mdivi-1 restores mitochondrial morphology and attenuates hypoxia resistance.

citation: Loss of hepatic DRP1 exacerbates alcoholic hepatitis by inducing megamitochondria and mitochondrial maladaptation (PMID: 35698731)
summary: Hepatic DRP1 is decreased in human alcoholic hepatitis and in alcohol-fed mice, because alcohol impairs TFEB-mediated induction of DNM1L. Liver-specific DRP1 knockout causes megamitochondria, reduced mitophagy, cytosolic mtDNA and cGAS-STING-interferon activation, with increased liver injury and inflammation.

citation: ASHG 2015 - Missense mutations in the middle domain of DNM1L cause infantile encephalopathy in humans and peroxisomal and mitochondrial defects in Drosophila and humans
summary: Human wild-type DNM1L rescues Drosophila drp1 mutants. The p.G350R and p.A395D middle-domain variants instead produce aggregated mitochondria with trafficking defects in fly neurons, supporting their pathogenicity in patients with encephalopathy.

citation: ASHG 2016 - DNM1L-related mitochondrial fission defect presenting as spastic paraparesis and optic atrophy
summary: A de novo heterozygous DNM1L p.Thr59Ile variant in the GTPase domain was found in a patient with spastic paraparesis, cerebellar syndrome and optic atrophy. Patient myoblasts showed mega-mitochondria along an elongated mitochondrial network, and muscle biopsy showed mild CI+III and COX defects.

citation: Reversibility and therapeutic feasibility of DNM1L-associated neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 41786974)
summary: Expressing DNM1L variants in developing mouse brain caused severe neuronal loss at the early postnatal stage. In a human stem-cell model with chemogenetic control of DNM1L, over 75% of the pathological transcriptional changes were reversible even in differentiated neurons. Targeting mitochondrial biogenesis prevented neurodegeneration.

citation: Clinically diverse and perinatally lethal syndromes with urorectal septum malformation sequence (PMID: 36478354)
phenotype: urorectal septum malformation sequence (fetus); multiple congenital anomalies (perinatal lethal)
diagnostic_reason: Heterozygous missense variants classified as variants of uncertain significance (PM2, absent from controls, predicted deleterious in silico); causality not established. Genome sequencing was reported as nondiagnostic.

citation: Clinically diverse and perinatally lethal syndromes with urorectal septum malformation sequence (PMID: 36478354)
phenotype: urorectal septum malformation sequence (fetus); multiple congenital anomalies (perinatal lethal)
diagnostic_reason: Heterozygous missense variants classified as variants of uncertain significance (PM2, absent from controls, predicted deleterious in silico); causality not established. Genome sequencing was reported as nondiagnostic.

citation: Prenatal exome sequencing analysis in fetal structural anomalies detected by ultrasonography (PAGE): a cohort study (PMID: 30712880)
variant_detail: NALCN missense variant (specific change not given in the abstract; fetus PP3387)
phenotype: multisystem fetal structural anomalies
diagnostic_reason: Presumed de novo heterozygous missense variant in a developmental disorder gene, reviewed by a clinical review panel and listed as a diagnostic variant.
center_country: England and Scotland, UK (Birmingham and London fetal medicine units)

citation: Lu et al. 2007 - The neuronal channel NALCN contributes resting sodium permeability and is required for normal respiratory rhythm (PMID: 17448995)
phenotype: severely disrupted respiratory rhythm; neonatal death within 24 hours of birth; reduced neuronal firing in brainstem-spinal cord preparations; absent TTX- and Cs+-resistant background Na+ leak current in hippocampal neurons; resting membrane potential insensitive to changes in extracellular Na+

citation: Lu et al. 2010 - Extracellular calcium controls background current and neuronal excitability via an UNC79-UNC80-NALCN cation channel complex (PMID: 21040849)
phenotype: in nalcn and unc79 knockout neuron cultures, the Na+-leak current (IL-Na) is insensitive to changes in extracellular Ca2+; reducing extracellular Ca2+ fails to produce the excitatory effects seen in wild-type neurons

citation: Lu et al. 2010 - Genetic analysis of mouse strains with variable serum sodium concentrations identifies the Nalcn sodium channel as a novel player in osmoregulation (PMID: 21177381)
phenotype: hypernatremia (elevated serum sodium) in heterozygous Nalcn knockout mice compared with wild-type littermates; Nalcn locus on chromosome 14 associated with serum sodium levels across 27 inbred strains

citation: Hernandez et al. 2018 - Na+-Leak Channel, Non-Selective (NALCN) Regulates Myometrial Excitability and Facilitates Successful Parturition (PMID: 30021195)
phenotype: smooth-muscle-specific NALCN knockout (NALCNfx/fx x MHC-Cre); reduced myometrial excitability with shortened action potential bursts; increased rate of abnormal labor, including prolonged and dysfunctional labor

citation: Philippart & Khaliq 2018 - Gi/o protein-coupled receptors in dopamine neurons inhibit the sodium leak channel NALCN (PMID: 30556810)
phenotype: D2 receptor-mediated inhibition of sodium leak currents lost in NALCN conditional knockout dopaminergic neurons; NALCN knockout dopaminergic neurons mainly silent, whereas nearly all wild-type neurons fire spontaneously; GABA-B receptor inhibition of NALCN-mediated currents

citation: Contributions of the Sodium Leak Channel NALCN to Pacemaking of Medial Ventral Tegmental Area and Substantia Nigra Dopaminergic Neurons (PMID: 37640554)
phenotype: in SNc DANs, speeding of pacemaking by low extracellular Ca2+ seen in wild-type but not NALCN conditional knockout mice; NALCN inhibition (pharmacological) slowed pacemaking in VTA DAN subpopulations but not in SNc DANs

citation: Deletion of the sodium leak channel NALCN in dopamine neurons alters D2R-mediated signalling and psychostimulant responsiveness (PMID: 42837280)
phenotype: dampened tonic activity of VTA DA neurons; unchanged basal extracellular DA in nucleus accumbens; no impairment of basal motor responses or reactivity to threat-predicting cues; enhanced neurochemical and behavioural responses to psychostimulants; altered presynaptic D2R-mediated signalling at DA terminals

citation: NALCN channels enhance the intrinsic excitability of spinal projection neurons (PMID: 29746349)
phenotype: genetic deletion of NALCN reduced intrinsic excitability of lamina I spino-PB neurons; knockout of NALCN prevented substance P-evoked action potential discharge in spino-PB neurons

citation: The Na(+) leak channel NALCN controls spontaneous activity and mediates synaptic modulation by α2-adrenergic receptors in auditory neurons (PMID: 38197879)
phenotype: glycinergic neuron-specific NALCN knockout; loss of spontaneous firing in cartwheel cells; absent α2-adrenergic and GABAB receptor modulation of firing; absent α2-dependent enhancement of synaptic strength

citation: Effects of NALCN-Encoded Na(+) Leak Currents on the Repetitive Firing Properties of SCN Neurons Depend on K(+)-Driven Rhythmic Changes in Input Resistance (PMID: 37339878)
phenotype: in vivo conditional NALCN knockout selectively reduced daytime repetitive firing rates of adult SCN neurons

citation: Intellectual disability-associated UNC80 mutations reveal inter-subunit interaction and dendritic function of the NALCN channel complex (PMID: 32620897)
phenotype: UNC80 (NALCN complex subunit) knockout mice are neonatal lethal

citation: Structural architecture of the human NALCN channelosome (PMID: 34929720)
summary: Cryo-EM structure of the ~1-MDa NALCN channelosome. UNC79 and UNC80 form an intertwined HEAT-repeat superhelix that docks intracellularly onto the NALCN-FAM155A pore subcomplex. Calmodulin co-purifies bound to the NALCN C-terminal domain, and the UNC79-UNC80 assembly contacts the NALCN DI-DII and DII-DIII linkers. Single-channel recordings showed a low open probability for the wild-type complex.

citation: Architecture of the human NALCN channelosome (PMID: 35387979)
summary: UNC79-UNC80 associates with the NALCN-FAM155A subcomplex through the intracellular II-III linker of NALCN. Disrupting the UNC79-UNC80 interface or the II-III linker interaction significantly reduced NALCN currents in HEK293T cells. Cross-linking mass spectrometry identified calmodulin bound to the NALCN C-terminal domain.

citation: Functional expression of CLIFAHDD and IHPRF pathogenic variants of the NALCN channel in neuronal cells (PMID: 31409833)
summary: In NG108-15 neuronal cells, wild-type NALCN current was carried by Na+, blocked by Gd3+, TTX-insensitive, and potentiated by low external Ca2+. It also showed time-dependent inactivation and voltage sensitivity. The IHPRF mutant W1287L gave no current (loss of function). The CLIFAHDD mutants L509S and Y578S gave higher current densities and slower inactivation (gain of function).

citation: Methylation determines the extracellular calcium sensitivity of the leak channel NALCN in hippocampal dentate granule cells (PMID: 31601786)
summary: PRMT7 methylates NALCN at Arg1653 in the C-terminus. Loss of this methylation reduces CaSR/PKC-delta-mediated phosphorylation of Ser1652 and relieves [Ca2+]e-dependent NALCN inhibition. This increases NALCN activity and neuronal excitability. PRMT7-/- dentate granule cells had a depolarized resting membrane potential and hyperexcitability.

citation: TRPC3 and NALCN channels drive pacemaking in substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons (PMID: 34409942)
summary: NALCN and TRPC3 together form the sustained inward currents behind slow depolarization and pacemaking in nigral dopamine neurons. Blocking NALCN abolished pacemaking in both wild-type and TRPC3 KO mice. NALCN current and mRNA/protein were upregulated in TRPC3 KO mice, indicating compensation.

citation: Progesterone and estrogen regulate NALCN expression in human myometrial smooth muscle cells (PMID: 31935111)
summary: In human myometrial smooth muscle cells, estrogen decreased NALCN mRNA 2.3-fold and protein, while progesterone increased mRNA 5.6-fold and restored protein. Progesterone enhanced and estrogen inhibited the NALCN-dependent leak current. Luciferase assays showed that progesterone response elements in the NALCN promoter drive the regulation, whereas the estrogen response element does not.

citation: The transcription factor unc-130/FOXD3/4 contributes to the biphasic calcium response required to optimize avoidance behavior (PMID: 35115609)
summary: In C. elegans, the transcription factor unc-130 (FOXD3/4 ortholog) upregulates expression of nca-2, the NALCN homolog, along with glr-1 and eat-4 in AIB central neurons. This supports the calcium responses needed to optimize avoidance behavior.

citation: The NALCN channel regulates metastasis and nonmalignant cell dissemination (PMID: 36175792)
summary: NALCN loss-of-function mutations were enriched in human gastric and colorectal cancers among 10,022 tumors. Nalcn deletion in mouse tumors, or treatment with gadolinium (a NALCN blocker), increased circulating tumor cells and metastases without changing tumor incidence. Nalcn deletion in non-cancer mice also caused epithelial cell shedding into the blood.

citation: De novo mutations in NALCN cause a syndrome characterized by congenital contractures of the limbs and face, hypotonia, and developmental delay (PMID: 25683120)
summary: Exome sequencing and molecular-inversion-probe screening found 14 de novo missense NALCN mutations clustered in or near the S5/S6 pore segments in CLIFAHDD families. In vitro, the variants nearly abolished expression of wild-type NALCN, suggesting a dominant-negative effect. This contrasts with recessive NALCN mutations elsewhere in the gene, which cause hypotonia and intellectual disability.

citation: Rapid molecular evolution of pain insensitivity in multiple African rodents (PMID: 31147513)
summary: The AITC-insensitive highveld mole-rat overexpresses NALCN in nociceptors, which ablates AITC detection. This identifies NALCN overexpression as a mechanism that shuts down pain signaling.

citation: Grandparental genotyping enhances exome variant interpretation (PMID: 32027463)
variant_detail: Pathogenic/likely pathogenic SOX10 variant (exact notation not given in abstract); apparently inherited from an unaffected parent but shown to be de novo in the grandparent generation
phenotype: Phenotype not specified in abstract; Parent reported as unaffected
diagnostic_reason: Pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant identified on trio exome. Grandparental segregation showed the variant was de novo in the parent (apparent parental mosaicism or de novo event), explaining the parent's lack of symptoms.

citation: 22q12.3-q13.1 microdeletion including SOX10 causes atypical Waardenburg syndrome (PMID: 32703023)
variant_detail: 1.99 Mb deletion arr[hg19]22q12.3-13.1 (chr22:36656004-38643920) including SOX10 and 13 other RefSeq genes
phenotype: Atypical Waardenburg syndrome; Severe congenital heart disease; Strabismus; Iris pigment disturbance/heterochromia
diagnostic_reason: Heterozygous contiguous deletion encompassing SOX10, interpreted as acting as a dominant pathogenic variant. Family exome testing was performed.

citation: Clinical, endocrinological, and molecular characterization of Kallmann syndrome and normosmic idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism: a single center experience (PMID: 25883924)
variant_detail: SOX10 variant(s) identified in a small number of patients (exact notation not given in abstract). Together with KAL1 and CHD7, molecular defects were found in 5 patients from 4 families.
phenotype: Kallmann syndrome / isolated GnRH deficiency; Hearing loss (SOX10 was tested in patients with CHARGE features or deafness); Absent or hypoplastic olfactory bulb/sulci
diagnostic_reason: SOX10 was analyzed in patients with deafness or CHARGE features, and a molecular defect was identified in SOX10 in at least one patient.

citation: Interactions between Sox10 and EdnrB modulate penetrance and severity of aganglionosis in the Sox10Dom mouse model of Hirschsprung disease (PMID: 15294878)
phenotype: Enteric aganglionosis with variable penetrance and expressivity depending on genetic background; C57BL/6J EdnrB alleles increased penetrance and severity of aganglionosis in Sox10Dom/+ mice; Sox10/EdnrB double mutants showed significantly more severe aganglionosis; The background strain of the EdnrB mutant further modified the phenotype of double mutants
knockout_type: heterozygous knockout (Sox10Dom spontaneous mutant allele; Sox10Dom/+ crossed with EdnrB mutants)
significance: highly significant effect of EdnrB alleles (no specific p-value given in abstract)

citation: Control of cranial ectomesenchyme fate by Nr2f nuclear receptors (PMID: 36367707)
phenotype: nr2f5 and nr2f2;nr2f5 mutants showed delayed downregulation of sox10 and delayed upregulation of ectomesenchyme genes; Mutation of sox10 fully rescued skeletal development in nr2f5 single mutants; sox10 mutation did not rescue skeletal development in nr2f2;nr2f5 double mutants; Initial ectomesenchyme delay persisted in both single and double mutants despite sox10 loss
knockout_type: full knockout (sox10 mutation combined with nr2f5 single and nr2f2;nr2f5 double mutants)

citation: ASHG 2014 - Additive toxicity of SOX10 mutation underlies a complex neurological phenotype of PCWH
phenotype: Delayed integration of Schwann cells in the sciatic nerve; Delayed terminal differentiation of oligodendrocytes in the spinal cord; Hypomyelination in the PNS and CNS; Neurosensory deafness; Abnormal skin pigmentation (melanocyte defects); Loss of the enteric nervous system; Phenotype severity increased with transgene copy number (dosage effect)
knockout_type: other (BAC transgenic expressing PCWH-causing SOX10 c.1400del12 mutant in Sox10-expressing cells; dominant toxic gain-of-function model)

citation: ASHG 2010 - Sox10 BAC transgenic mouse modeling a complex neurocristopathy, PCWH
phenotype: Circling behavior; Hypopigmented coat color; Neurosensory deafness; Abnormal enlargement of colon; Abnormal motor coordination; Relatively normal migration and differentiation of oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells but delayed myelination
knockout_type: other (BAC transgenic expressing PCWH-causing mutant Sox10)

citation: Adult sox10(+) Cardiomyocytes Contribute to Myocardial Regeneration in the Zebrafish (PMID: 31644901)
phenotype: Genetic ablation of sox10+ cardiomyocytes impaired cardiac regeneration after cryoinjury; sox10+ cardiomyocyte subset expanded after cryoinjury
knockout_type: other (genetic ablation of sox10+ cardiomyocytes; fate mapping)

citation: Control of cranial ectomesenchyme fate by Nr2f nuclear receptors (PMID: 36367707)
summary: In zebrafish, nr2f5 and nr2f2;nr2f5 mutants fail to downregulate sox10, which is normally restricted to early neural crest and non-ectomesenchyme lineages. Mutating sox10 fully rescued skeletal development in nr2f5 single mutants but not in double mutants. Sox10 perdurance therefore antagonizes the ectomesenchyme transition but does not explain the Nr2f-dependent delay.

citation: Sox10 Functions as an Inducer of the Direct Conversion of Keratinocytes Into Neural Crest Cells (PMID: 33040687)
summary: Sox10 overexpression converted bone marrow mesenchymal cells, but not keratinocytes, into P75+ neural crest cells. Keratinocytes converted when Sox10 was co-expressed with Snail1, Snail2, Twist1 and Tcfap2a. Sox10 expressed after the four factors produced multipotent neural crest cells, so the order of expression matters.

citation: ASHG 2023 - Genetic epistasis between RET and ELP1 explains gastrointestinal motility dysfunction in Familial Dysautonomia patients
summary: Sox10 expression is altered in both Ret and Elp1 knockout mouse embryonic gut (scRNA-seq, E14.5). In SK-N-SH cells, ELP1 heterozygous knockout reduced SOX10 by about 15%, and RET heterozygous knockout reduced SOX10 by about 80%. SOX10 therefore sits in a shared gene regulatory network with RET, ELP1 and EDNRB in the enteric nervous system.

citation: ASHG 2016 - Investigating the role of SOX10-regulated alternative promoter use in Schwann cells
sample_size: 10,679 putative TSSs; 407 novel TSSs; 55 SOX10-bound promoters
summary: Integrating CAGE data with SOX10 ChIP-seq identified 55 previously unannotated promoters bound by SOX10 in Schwann cells. SOX10 is necessary and sufficient for activity of an alternative MTMR2 promoter and expression of its transcript, which encodes a protein isoform with different nuclear localization.

citation: ASHG 2016 - Investigating the role of SOX6 during the development of the peripheral nervous system
summary: SOX10 activates SOX6 through an intronic alternative promoter. Deleting the SOX10 consensus sites reduced promoter activity in Schwann cells, and SOX10 expression in SOX10-negative motor neurons induced the promoter and endogenous SOX6 transcription. SOX6 may in turn repress a subset of SOX10 targets to maintain a premyelinating state.

citation: ASHG 2015 - SOX10 Regulates an Alternative Promoter at the Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Locus MTMR2
summary: SOX10 drives a Schwann cell-specific alternative MTMR2 promoter. Ectopic SOX10 induced the endogenous transcript in a heterologous cell line, and impairing SOX10 function nearly ablated it in Schwann cells. The resulting N-terminally truncated MTMR2 isoform shows higher nuclear localization, which may be relevant to CMT4B1.

citation: SOX10: 20 years of phenotypic plurality and current understanding of its developmental function (PMID: 34667088)
summary: SOX10 is a transcription factor of the SOX family. Heterozygous mutations cause Waardenburg syndrome types 2 and 4, PCWH, intestinal pseudo-obstruction, Kallmann syndrome and isolated hearing loss. SOX10 regulates neural crest derivatives (melanocytes, enteric nervous system, Schwann cells, olfactory ensheathing cells) and the inner ear and oligodendrocytes.

citation: Rapid and efficient generation of oligodendrocytes from human induced pluripotent stem cells using transcription factors (PMID: 28246330)
summary: Induced expression of SOX10, OLIG2 and NKX6.2 in iPSC-derived neural progenitors rapidly generated O4+ oligodendrocytes with up to 70% efficiency in 28 days. The cells resembled primary human oligodendrocytes and myelinated the CNS of Mbp shi/shi Rag-/- mice.

citation: SOX10-dependent CMTM7 expression inhibits cell proliferation and tumor growth in gastric carcinoma (PMID: 30392914)
summary: SOX10 and CMTM7 are both down-regulated in gastric cancer tissue and their expression is correlated (r=0.6455). SOX10 transcriptionally regulates CMTM7 in luciferase assays. SOX10 overexpression in CMTM7-silenced cells inhibited proliferation and tumor growth.

citation: ADRB2 inhibition suppresses cancer immune evasion by regulating tumor SOX10-PD-L1 axis and T cell function (PMID: 40514069)
summary: ADRB2 signaling through PKA upregulates SOX10, which transcriptionally regulates PD-L1 (shown by luciferase reporter and ChIP-PCR). SOX10 knockdown mimicked ADRB2 inhibition and SOX10 overexpression reversed it. The axis was conserved in colorectal cancer models.

citation: Qiao et al. 2021 - Rare and de novo variants in 827 congenital diaphragmatic hernia probands implicate LONP1 as candidate risk gene (PMID: 34547244)
variant_detail: Not specified in abstract; de novo damaging variants in ALYREF identified in CDH probands (number of carriers and variant details not given)
phenotype: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia
diagnostic_reason: Enrichment of de novo damaging variants in ALYREF in 827 CDH proband-parent trios; significant at FDR < 0.05, identifying ALYREF as a candidate CDH risk gene
center_country: Columbia University, USA (CDH study consortium, multicenter)

citation: ASHG 2022 - Integrated genetic analysis of transcriptome sequencing data in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (Qiao et al.)
variant_detail: Putative pathogenic ALYREF variant (details not given); RNA-seq of diaphragm cells showed functional effect (aberrant splicing/RNA processing)
phenotype: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia
diagnostic_reason: RNA-seq of diaphragm tissue showed functional effects of ALYREF variant on RNA processing, supporting pathogenicity of putative pathogenic de novo variant

citation: The Role of De Novo Variants in Patients with Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia (PMID: 34573387)
variant_detail: De novo ALYREF variant (chr17: 81,887,835–81,891,586 locus), detected by trio WES/WGS; details not given, citing ref 12
phenotype: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia
diagnostic_reason: De novo variant identified by trio WES/WGS in a CDH patient (review summarizing previously published data)

citation: Incomplete activation of Alyref and Gabpb1 leads to preimplantation arrest in cloned mouse embryos (PMID: 37640449)
phenotype: Early developmental (preimplantation) arrest after CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of Alyref; Improper inner cell mass formation, via dysregulation of Nanog; Alyref mRNA supplementation rescued preimplantation development of cloned (NT) embryos

citation: Alyref Deficiency Exacerbates Chronic Inflammatory Pain by Impairing Nuclear Export of Ccn3 MRNA (PMID: 42242915)
phenotype: Conditional deletion of Alyref in NaV1.8+ nociceptive neurons exacerbated CFA-induced thermal and cold hypersensitivity, mechanical allodynia and hyperalgesia; Increased microglial and astrocyte activation in the spinal dorsal horn; Elevated proinflammatory mediators and MMP-9; Impaired nuclear export of Ccn3 mRNA and reduced Ccn3 expression in DRG neurons

citation: ALYREF stabilizes MZF1 via m5C modification to exacerbate cardiac remodeling and atrial fibrillation in heart failure (PMID: 42249105)
phenotype: In ISO-induced heart failure model, Alyref knockdown reduced MZF1 and HTRA1 expression; Alleviated myocardial hypertrophy, fibrosis and cardiac dysfunction; Reduced atrial fibrillation inducibility

citation: ALYREF drives NLRP3 inflammasome-dependent macrophage pyroptosis to promote sepsis-associated acute liver injury by enhancing GADD45A mRNA stability (PMID: 42425434)
phenotype: Alyref knockdown inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome-dependent macrophage pyroptosis; Alleviated sepsis-associated acute liver injury in the CLP model; Reduced GADD45A expression

citation: NEDD4L-mediated ALYREF ubiquitination degradation suppresses RUBCNL expression to impair autophagy and promote lipogenesis in alcoholic hepatic fibrosis (PMID: 42715837)
phenotype: AAV-mediated ALYREF silencing in AHF mice partially reversed the protective effects of NEDD4L depletion; Reduced RUBCNL, impaired autophagy, lipid accumulation and fibrosis in the AHF context

citation: ALYREF Promotes Progression of Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma through Increasing the Level of Isocitrate Dehydrogenase 1 in an m5C-Dependent Manner (PMID: 40369958)
phenotype: ALYREF knockdown in a xenograft tumor model significantly suppressed tumor growth

citation: Wang et al. 2024 - The molecular chaperone ALYREF promotes R-loop resolution and maintains genome stability (PMID: 39547511)
summary: Purified ALYREF binds DNA-RNA hybrids and R-loops and stimulates UAP56-mediated R-loop dissociation in vitro, which depends on its interaction with UAP56 and R-loops. ALYREF depletion in cells causes R-loop accumulation and R-loop-mediated genome instability, so ALYREF acts as an R-loop coregulator.

citation: MicroRNA sequence codes for small extracellular vesicle release and cellular retention (PMID: 34937935)
summary: The RNA-binding proteins Alyref and Fus are involved in exporting miRNAs that carry the EXOmotif CGGGAG into small extracellular vesicles. This identifies a role for Alyref in sorting miRNAs for secretion.

citation: The role of the HIF-1α/ALYREF/PKM2 axis in glycolysis and tumorigenesis of bladder cancer (PMID: 33991457)
summary: ALYREF binds m5C sites in the PKM2 3'UTR and stabilizes PKM2 mRNA, and its overexpression promotes bladder cancer proliferation through PKM2-mediated glycolysis. HIF-1α activates ALYREF, which makes ALYREF part of a HIF-1α/ALYREF/PKM2 axis. High ALYREF and PKM2 predicted poor patient survival.

citation: Aging-declined RNA exportation impairs hematopoietic stem cells by inducing R-loop (PMID: 40605703)
summary: Alyref, the main TREX component, declines in aged hematopoietic stem cells, which causes nuclear RNA retention, R-loop formation, replication stress and DNA damage. Restoring Alyref in aged HSCs rescues RNA export, reduces R-loops and replication stress, and improves HSC function.

citation: NSUN4 mediated RNA 5-methylcytosine promotes the malignant progression of glioma through improving the CDC42 mRNA stabilization (PMID: 38876383)
summary: NSUN4-mediated m5C modification promotes ALYREF binding to CDC42 mRNA and stabilizes it. CDC42 then activates PI3K-AKT signaling to drive glioma proliferation, migration and invasion in vitro and in vivo.

citation: Epigenetic addition of m(5)C to HBV transcripts promotes viral replication and evasion of innate antiviral responses (PMID: 38216565)
summary: The m5C site at nt 1291 of HBV mRNA is required for ALYREF recognition, which promotes viral mRNA export and HBx translation. NSUN2 catalyzes the m5C addition.

citation: 5-Methylcytosine RNA Modifications Promote Retrovirus Replication in an ALYREF Reader Protein-Dependent Manner (PMID: 32321818)
summary: ALYREF functions as an m5C reader that regulates murine leukemia virus replication, and MLV genomic RNA is highly enriched for m5C.

citation: ALYREF m5C RNA methylation reader predicts bladder cancer prognosis by regulating the tumor immune microenvironment (PMID: 38579085)
summary: ALYREF mRNA and protein are upregulated in bladder cancer, and immunofluorescence shows it localizes mainly to nuclear speckles. Among the m5C regulators, only ALYREF was significantly correlated with overall survival, and it is associated with macrophage infiltration.

citation: TREX tetramer disruption alters RNA processing necessary for corticogenesis in THOC6 Intellectual Disability Syndrome (PMID: 38388531)
summary: Biallelic THOC6 loss-of-function variants reduce the binding affinity of ALYREF to THOC5 without changing TREX protein levels, which implicates impaired TREX tetramer formation. The neural phenotype involves mis-splicing rather than detectable mRNA export defects.

citation: HnRNPA2B1 ISGylation Regulates m6A-Tagged mRNA Selective Export via ALYREF/NXF1 Complex to Foster Breast Cancer Development (PMID: 38626369)
summary: hnRNPA2B1 acts as an m6A reader and exports m6A-tagged mRNAs through the ALYREF/NXF1 complex, which promotes stemness gene expression in breast cancer stem cells.

citation: ASHG 2012 - Cardiac Malformations Associated With Germline WT1 Mutations in Children Presenting With Wilms' Tumour. (S. Bowdin, C. Owens, D. Malkin, N. Parkinson, M. Friedburg, R. Grant)
variant_detail: Germline WT1 mutations or 11p13 genomic abnormalities (specific variants not given); 5 of 12 patients with adequate cardiac data had cardiac findings
phenotype: Wilms' tumor; complete transposition of the great arteries; ventricular septal defect (VSD); atrial septal defect (ASD); atrial tachycardia; right-sided aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery; WAGR syndrome (2 patients; 1 with normal cardiac findings, 1 with insufficient cardiac information)
diagnostic_reason: Known germline WT1 mutations or 11p13 deletions in children with Wilms' tumor; retrospective review suggests an increased incidence of congenital heart defects.
center_country: The Hospital for Sick Children, Toronto, Canada

citation: Genotype-phenotype analysis of pediatric patients with WT1 glomerulopathy (PMID: 27300205)
variant_detail: WT1 missense mutations (n=11; specific variants not given in abstract)
phenotype: congenital/infantile nephrotic syndrome (9/11); steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome; ESRD in all (median age 2.6 months); disorders of sexual development in 46,XY patients; Wilms tumor (1 patient in cohort); diaphragmatic defect/hernia (3 patients in cohort)
diagnostic_reason: Genetic screening of WT1 in children with steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome; genotype-phenotype correlation (missense vs KTS splice)

citation: Genotype-phenotype analysis of pediatric patients with WT1 glomerulopathy (PMID: 27300205)
variant_detail: WT1 KTS splicing mutations (n=10; intron 9 donor site, specific variants not given in abstract)
phenotype: childhood-onset steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (8/10); ESRD in 5 patients (median age 9.3 years); disorders of sexual development in 46,XY patients; gonadoblastoma (1 patient in cohort)
diagnostic_reason: Genetic screening of WT1 in children with steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome; genotype-phenotype correlation (missense vs KTS splice)

citation: Diaphragmatic hernia in Denys-Drash syndrome (PMID: 7645607)
variant_detail: c.1097G>A, p.Arg366His
phenotype: male pseudohermaphroditism; glomerular lesions (Denys-Drash syndrome); no Wilms tumor; large diaphragmatic hernia
diagnostic_reason: Constitutional heterozygous WT1 mutation in a newborn with Denys-Drash syndrome; WT1 expression in mesothelium and the mouse knockout diaphragmatic hernia support causality

citation: WT1 splice-site mutations are rarely associated with primary steroid-resistant focal and segmental glomerulosclerosis (PMID: 10792605)
variant_detail: IVS9 c.1228+4C>T (1228+4 C>T) heterozygous donor splice-site
phenotype: steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome with FSGS; diaphragmatic hernia; proximal hypospadias; unilateral testicular ectopia; reduced +KTS/-KTS ratio (0.43)
diagnostic_reason: Intron 9 splice-site mutation altering the +KTS/-KTS ratio, identical to that of Frasier syndrome patients (controls 1.50-2.00)

citation: Denys-Drash syndrome and congenital diaphragmatic hernia: another case with the 1097G > A(Arg366His) mutation (PMID: 18203154)
variant_detail: c.1097G>A, p.Arg366His
phenotype: congenital diaphragmatic hernia; Denys-Drash syndrome features
diagnostic_reason: Recurrent Arg366His WT1 mutation, previously reported in two other CDH cases with DDS

citation: Hydrothorax in a patient with Denys-Drash syndrome associated with a diaphragmatic defect (PMID: 16932893)
variant_detail: p.Arg366His heterozygous
phenotype: typical Denys-Drash syndrome; chronic renal failure; diaphragmatic defect detected after peritoneal dialysis; hydrothorax
diagnostic_reason: Heterozygous WT1 missense mutation in an infant with typical Denys-Drash syndrome

citation: Exome sequencing of fetuses with congenital diaphragmatic hernia supports a causal role for NR2F2, PTPN11, and WT1 variants (PMID: 34315577)
variant_detail: Likely damaging WT1 variant (specific variant not given in abstract)
phenotype: congenital diaphragmatic hernia (fetal)
diagnostic_reason: Rare variant classified as Likely Damaging on trio exome sequencing; WT1 is also implicated in other CDH cohorts

citation: Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia and Congenital Nephrotic Syndrome in a Low-Birth-Weight Infant: A Case Report (PMID: 41142893)
variant_detail: c.1316G>A, p.Arg439His (exon 8)
phenotype: congenital diaphragmatic hernia; congenital nephrotic syndrome; progressive acute kidney injury requiring dialysis; low birth weight; ascites; death at 74 days
diagnostic_reason: Genetic testing confirmed a WT1 missense mutation in an infant with congenital nephrotic syndrome and CDH

citation: Wilm's tumor 1 promotes memory flexibility (PMID: 31434897)
phenotype: WT1 knockdown enhanced CA1 neuronal excitability, LTP and long-term memory; WT1 overexpression weakened memory retention; Forebrain WT1-deficient mice showed deficits in reversal learning and sequential learning tasks; Impaired contextual fear extinction, indicating impaired memory flexibility
knockout_type: conditional knockout (forebrain-specific WT1-deficient mice) plus hippocampal knockdown

citation: WT1 directs normal progesterone receptor-chromatin binding essential for uterine receptivity at peri-implantation (PMID: 40627402)
phenotype: Implantation failure; Attenuated progesterone responsiveness in uterine stromal cells; Aberrant uterine receptivity; Impaired PR-chromatin binding and reduced transcription of PR target genes

citation: Activation of podocyte Notch mediates early Wt1 glomerulopathy (PMID: 29398135)
phenotype: Podocyte apoptosis from day 4 post-induction; Glomerulosclerosis and albuminuria; Podocyte Notch activation (Notch1, Nrarp, Hey2, HES1 upregulated); FoxC2 repression; Podocyte EMT-related gene upregulation; Notch inhibition ameliorated glomerular scarring and albuminuria
knockout_type: conditional knockout (tamoxifen-inducible Cre-loxP deletion of Wt1 in adult mice)

citation: Alternatively spliced isoforms of WT1 control podocyte-specific gene expression (PMID: 25993318)
phenotype: A restricted set of genes was dependent on the +KTS isoform, including MAGI2; Podocyte differentiation defects; MAGI2α is needed for nephrin localization and slit diaphragm assembly; Reduced MAGI2 in LPS glomerular injury model
knockout_type: other (mice lacking the WT1 +KTS splice isoform)

citation: Wt1 transcription factor impairs cardiomyocyte specification and drives a phenotypic switch from myocardium to epicardium (PMID: 35312773)
phenotype: Sustained wt1b expression reduced chromatin accessibility; Cardiomyocytes delaminated from the myocardium and upregulated epicardial genes; Transdifferentiation into epicardial-like cells
knockout_type: other (ectopic/sustained wt1a and wt1b overexpression in cardiomyocytes; gain-of-function, not knockout)

citation: Dose-Dependent and Non-Autonomous Signaling in CAKUT: A Lineage-Specific Framework from Conditional Knockout Studies (PMID: 41897393)
phenotype: Defective nephrogenesis; Expansion of stromal progenitors; Pro-apoptotic phenotype with loss of Wt1, rescued by exogenous FGF; Loss of Wt1 impairs FGF signaling and increases BMP/pSMAD activity
knockout_type: conditional knockout (Six2-Cre-mediated Wt1 deletion in nephron progenitors; review)

citation: Autophagy regulates differentiation of ovarian granulosa cells through degradation of WT1 (PMID: 35025698)
summary: siRNA knockdown of ATG5 or BECN1, or chloroquine treatment, in granulosa cells caused WT1 to accumulate because autophagic degradation was insufficient. This reduced CYP19A1 and FSHR expression and estradiol synthesis. GCs from biochemical POI patients showed reduced autophagy markers.

citation: Epg5 deficiency leads to primary ovarian insufficiency due to WT1 accumulation in mouse granulosa cells (PMID: 35786405)
summary: Epg5 knockout mice showed a POI-like phenotype with blocked autophagic flux. WT1 accumulated in granulosa cells, which reduced steroidogenesis-related gene expression and impaired GC differentiation, indicating WT1 is selectively degraded by autophagy via EPG5.

citation: Inhibition of transcriptional coactivator YAP Impairs the expression and function of transcription factor WT1 in diabetic podocyte injury (PMID: 38423183)
summary: Podocyte-specific Yap knockout in diabetic mice decreased WT1 expression and the expression of WT1 targets, including Tead1. This places WT1 downstream of Hippo/YAP signaling in diabetic podocyte injury.

citation: TERT Expression in Wilms Tumor Is Regulated by Promoter Mutation or Hypermethylation, WT1, and N-MYC (PMID: 35406427)
summary: WTs with biallelic WT1 inactivating mutations (7/45) had lower TERT expression and telomerase activity. WT1 shRNA knockdown in WiT49 cells decreased TERT, colony formation and proliferation. An inducible Wt1 knockout in normal mouse nephrogenesis showed no effect on Tert, so the WT1-TERT coupling appears specific to transformed cells.

citation: WT1 recruits TET2 to regulate its target gene expression and suppress leukemia cell proliferation (PMID: 25601757)
summary: WT1 physically interacts with TET2 and recruits it to WT1 target genes to activate their expression. WT1 mutations are mutually exclusive with TET2/IDH1/IDH2 mutations in AML. AML-derived TET2 mutations disrupt the interaction, and TET2 suppression of leukemia cell proliferation depends on WT1.

citation: Alternatively spliced isoforms of WT1 control podocyte-specific gene expression (PMID: 25993318)
summary: ChIP-seq showed that almost half of podocyte-specific genes are direct WT1 targets, with FOXC1 binding sites near WT1-bound regions. Mice lacking the +KTS isoform showed altered expression of a restricted gene set including MAGI2, which is needed for nephrin localization and slit diaphragm assembly.

citation: WT1 and its transcriptional cofactor BASP1 redirect the differentiation pathway of an established blood cell line (PMID: 21269271)
summary: BASP1 is recruited to WT1-binding sites and suppresses WT1-mediated transcriptional activation. In K562 cells, WT1 and BASP1 together diverted PMA-induced differentiation to a neuronal-like phenotype.

citation: Antagonistic activities of CDC14B and CDK1 on USP9X regulate WT1-dependent mitotic transcription and survival (PMID: 32152317)
summary: WT1 was identified as a substrate that is deubiquitylated and stabilized by CDK1-phosphorylated USP9X (S2563) in mitosis. WT1 acts as a mitotic transcription factor and drives expression of its target CXCL8/IL-8, which conveys mitotic survival. CDC14B antagonizes this pathway.

citation: Classification of a frameshift/extended and a stop mutation in WT1 as gain-of-function mutations that activate cell cycle genes and promote Wilms tumour cell proliferation (PMID: 24619359)
summary: In Wilms tumour cell lines, mutant WT1 (p.V432fsX87 and p.P362X) showed gain-of-function activity. It upregulated G2/M cell cycle genes needed for proliferation, interacted physically with p53, and antagonized p53-mediated repression.

citation: ASHG 2016 - Pleiotropic effects of noncoding variants near EFEMP1, WT1, ADAMTS6, and EBF2 on the risk of abdominal hernias
summary: Noncoding variants at the WT1 locus were associated with inguinal hernia risk and with umbilical, femoral and ventral hernias. WT1 is expressed in mouse connective tissue, and pathway analysis suggests it influences connective tissue homeostasis through extracellular matrix enzymes such as MMPs.
